I have no hesitation to reverse the judgment and decree of the last court of fact as the same has suffered from serious miscarriage of justice. The citations as referred by the learned Advocate in support of his contentions are fully applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.</u>

23. In that view of the matter the impugned judgment and decree dated 11.11.1999 and 18.11.1999 respectively passed by the Subordinate Judge now Joint District Judge, 2"1 Court, Tangail reversing those of passed by the Assistant Judge, Madhupur, in Other Class Suit No.8 of 1997 dated 23.9.1998 and 29.9.1998 deserves my interference and accordingly . I find merit and substance in the Rule.

24. In the result, the Rule is hereby made absolute without any order as to costs.

25. The order of stay as granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

26. Send down the lower courts record along with a copy of this judgment to the concerned court forthwith for information and necessary action.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Md. Rabiul Karim, Advocate ------ For the petitioners 
Mr. Samarendra Nath Goswami, with Mr. Golam Mohammad Chowdhury, Advocates ------ For the Opposite parties
parties:
Sree Haripada Das and others ------ Petitioner
Versus
Haji Abbas Ali being dead his heirs: 1(a) Md. Kayem Ali Mirdha being dead his heirs: 1 (a)(i) Md. Fazhil Ho1ue Mridha and others ------ Opposite parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Shawkat Hussain .J:- The instant Rule arises at the instance of the judgment and decree dated 19.05.1993 and 25.05.1993 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Pabna in Other Appeal No. 124 of 1985 affirming the judgment and decree dated 20.05.1985 and 23.05.85 respectively passed by learned Munsif (now Assistant judge), Chatmohar , District-pabna in Other Suit No.5 of 1983 dismissing the suit. 

2. Plaintiffs case, in short, is that the suit land appertaining C.S Khatian No.308 of Monza of panchuria, P.S , Chatmohar, District- pabna originally belonged to plaintiff No. 1 and Radha Gobinda Das, the predecessor of plaintiff Nos.2 and 3, the two brothers in equal share who prior to partition in 1947 for the cause of communal riot lets this country and took shelter in west Bengal in India and as such the suit property came under the management of the Government of the then East Pakistan under tile provision of East Bengal Evacuee (Administration of immoveable properties) Act of 1951 and they. Without coming back to the country, used to manage the property through Ajahar Ali Akonda under the provision of East Bengal Evacuee Administration of Immoveable properties) Act of 1951: and thereafter Ajahar , All having been in possession of the same land in aforesaid manner for more than 12 years died leaving his sons who are in possession of the suit land on behalf of the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs at the death of Ajahar Ali appointed his son Aftab Hossain as Attorney on their behalf to manage the property by power of Attorney dated 22.12.1960. 

3. Defendant No. l having aware of the possession of the suit land as evacuee property under the management of Ajahar Ali Akonda collusively auction purchased on 02.08.1961 in certificate sale proceeding under Certificate Case No. 4039/1959-60 by practicing fraud and suppressing upon the plaintiffs. Ajahar Ali having aware of the certificate sale took it to the notice of plaintiff No.1 and his brother Radha Gobinda das and the plaintiff No.1 and Radha Gobinda Das who appointed Ajahar Ali as their constituted Attorney duly authenticated by Deputy High Commissioner or Pakistan at Calcutta and by virtue of power of Attorney Ajahar Ali Akonda filed a case for setting aside the Certificate Sale Case No.4039 of 1959-60 and pro-defendant No.2 set aside the auction sale and the order of the appellate Court is affirmed by the defendant No.1 but ultimately auction sale was affirmed by order dated 01.12.1977 on technical ground by the Joint-Secretary of the Government in Revisional application filed by the defendant No. 1 before Land Administration and Land Reforms Department. Subsequently, Radha Gobinda Das died leaving plaintiff Nos.2 and 3. Aftab Hossein as Attorney filed the instant suit on behalf of the plaintiffs for declaration that the Certificate Sale in Certificate Case No.4039 of 1959-60 is collusive, fraudulent. Void and it has no legal effect. 

4. On the contrary, the inter alia case of the defendant No. 1 is that Radha Gobinda Das and his brother Haripadha Das possessed the suit through their bargadars and they never left the country and for' arear of rent Certificate Case No.4039 of 1959-60 was instituted against them and at the time of certificate case they remained in the country and notice was duly severed upon them and the suit property was auction sold with their knowledge and defendant No. 1 duly purchased and got possession of the same on 23.12.1961 and remain in possession of the same by his own cultivation on payment of rents to the Government. Plaintiffs earlier filed the Case No.6577 for cancellation of auction sale and the case was disallowed by order dated 28.11.1977 and 01.12.1977. The plaintiffs have no locus-standi to file the instant suit. The suit has been filed on same fictitious ground to cause unnecessary harassment to the defendant. 

5. Defendant No.2, the vested property authority filed written statement and contested the suit by way of cross-examining the witnesses of the plaintiff and defendant claiming the suit land as vested and non-resident property. 

6. Trial Court M consideration of the facts of the pleadings and evidence on record dismissed the suit. The appellate Court also on hearing both the parties and appraisal of the facts of the case of the contending parties and evidence on record affirmed the judgment of the trial Court by the impugned judgment and decree and thereby the plaintiffs obtained the instant Rule. 

7. Mr. Md. Rabiul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners submits that the trial Court observed the irregularities in service of summons in the proceeding of the certificate sale but in spite of that both the Courts below dismissed the suit without setting aside the sale and thus committed error in law occasioning failure of justice. 

8. Mr, Md. Rabiul Karim further submits that plaintiffs duly filed the suit through their constituted Attorney but both the Courts below failed to appreciate the some thereby committed an error in law holding that the suit is not maintainable. 

9. Mr. Md. Rabiul karim also submits that the appellate Court did not apply his mind to the facts the case of the contend ending parties and evidence on record and affirmed the judgment of the trial Court mechanically on the reasoning and findings of the trial Court occasioning miscarriage of justice. 

10. Mr. Samarendra Nath Goswami with Mr. Golam Mohammed Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-respondent-opposite party submits that a concurrent finding of facts arrived at by the trial Court and the appellate Court cannot be disturbed in revision unless gross illegally is committed in appreciating the facts and misreading of evidence or any error of law or proceeding affecting the merit of the case. 

11. Mr. Samarendra Nath Goswami further submits that in the instant case trial court on proper appreciation of facts and evidence on record and on detail discussion dismissed the suit and appellate Court on applying its mind for the reasoning's and findings of the trial Court reached to its' agreement with the trial court and it does not necessarily require to give narration and reiteration of the reasons given by the trial Court. It the appellate Court arrived at a different from the findings of the trial Court, it had to asses both oral and documentary evidence to come to its independent finding. 

Mr. Samarendra Nath Goswami also submits that the impugned judgment and decree does not suffer from any illegality or infirmity and no occasion arises calling for any interference to it.

12. Mr. Samarendra Nath Goswami in support of his submission has referred decisions in the case Pulin Krishna Roy and Co-petitioners -Vs-president and Management committee of E.B. Evacuee property, Eden Buildings Dacca reported in 17 BLD-I62; Gurudas Saha-Vs-Deputy Custodian, Enemy Property (Land and Building) and others reported in 28 DLR-133; Md. Sadek Uddin Chowdhury and another Vs-Md. Anowarul Hoque Chowdhury and another reported in 11 BLT(HCD)-72 and Mrs. Razia Kader -Vs- Mrs. Nurun Nahar Begum reported in 8 BLT (HCD)-343. 

13. In the trial court plaintiffs examined 4 P.W.s and produced exhibits-1 to 10 P.W.s 1 and 2 are full brothers, the sons of Ajahar Ali alleged former Attorney P.Ws. 3 and 4 are witnesses relating to service of summons in the certificate proceeding and possession of the suit property. On the contrary defendant examined as many as 7 D.Ws and produced exhibits-A to G.

14. Defendant No.2 neither adduced any evidence nor produced any documentary evidence but contested the suit merely on cross-examining the witnesses of the plaintiffs as well as defendant. 

15. On perusal of the record, it appears that one Aftab Hossain as constituted Attorney on behalf of the plaintiffs filed the instant suit 10.01.1978 and he desposed on behalf of the plaintiffs as P.W.1 and in support of his appointment as Attorney; exhibit-6 a power of Attorney as allegedly executed by Haripada and others being authenticated by Notary Public in India has been filed. He claims that earlier his father was the Attorney on behalf of Haripada and Radhagobindo and the power of Attorney of his father remains with the office of A.D.C (Revenue) but, in fact, no such power of Attorney has been filed in the instant suit or it has called for from the office of A.D.C (Revenue). He (as P.W.I) admits that Haripada and Radhagobindo left for India before partition in 1947 at communal riot and they never came back to this country (the then East Pakistan) prior to 1965 or after 1965: No paper appears to show that he got the power Attorney, exhibit 6 through diplomatic chain He admits (as P.W.I) আমাকে যখন Power of Attorney দেয় তখন বাদীগণ নদীয়া জেলায় বসবাস করতো।” Neither the executanN nor any attesting witness appears to prove such power of Attorney. In fact, such power of Attorney, exhibit-6 has no validity in the eye of law. 

16. Admittedly Haripada and his brother Radhagobinda Das, the alleged plaintiffs left for India long before partition in 1947 and it does not appear that they ever returned to the East Pakistan even at declaration of Emergency in 1965 or at any time in emergence of Bangladesh and from admission of P.W.1 it appears that they both (including P.W.s 2 and 3 successors of Radhagobinda Das) remained there in India although and under the circumstances, they are.do doubt, aliens and the instant suit is barred under Section 83 of Civil procedure Code and the so-called Attorney Aftab Uddin has no locus-standi to institute such suit. It does not appear that the suit property was ever taken under the management of Evacuee property and the predecessor of Attorney managed the property on it's behalf. P.W.1 admits আমার ও আমার পিতার নাঃ জমির সাথে ব্যক্তিগত সম্পর্ক নাই। আমাকে প্রদত্ত আমমোক্তার কোথায় হয় জানিনা। আমি ঐ দলিল হওয়ার সময় উপস্থিত ছিলাম না। আমার পিতার আমমোক্তারের সময় আমি ছিলাম না। … ….. ….. নিলামের খবর পাওয়ার পর আমার বাবা ভারতে গিয়ে Power of Attorney নিয়ে আসে।
P.W. 2 also admits in the similar way “আমার পিতা চব্বিশ পরগনার রনীন্দ্রনগর গিয়ে Power of Attorney নিয়ে আসে।” 

17. It appears that both the courts below rightly held that the suit property was never in the management of Evacuee on management committee as under East Bengal Evacuee (Administration of Immovable property) Act 1951 and the suit being filed by so-called Attorney on behalf of alien citizens is not maintainable and the so called Attorney has no locus-standi to file the instant suit. 

18. Mr. Rabiul Karim could not appreciate the case of plaintiffs how the property came under the management of Evacuee management committee and what is the locus-standi of the so-called Attorney Aftab Uddin to institute the suit. 

19. In view of the discussion made herein before no reason appears to call for any interference to the concurrent findings of the courts below. 

20. In the result the instant Rule finds no merit. 

21. Accordingly, the Rule is discharged. 

22. No order as to cost. 

23. Send down the L.C. Record along with a copy of the judgment at once. 

End.

lawyer:
Mr. S. N. Goswami with Ms. Afsana Begum, Advocates ------ For the petitioners 
Mr. Khaled Ahmed with Mr. Md. Arifur Rahman, Advocates ------ For the respondent No.2
parties:
Radiant Garments Ltd. and another ------ Petitioners
Versus
Artha Rin Adalal and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Anwarul Haque, J.:  On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh this Rule nisi was issued calling the respondent Nos. 1-2 to show cause as to why the impugned Order No.10 dated 06.6.2006 passed by the Judge of the 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka in Artha Rin Case No.326 of 2005 and the prayer for rejection of application filed by the defendant under Section 21 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 shall not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. In short, the case of the petitioner for the purpose of disposal of the Rule is as follows:

Plaintiff, respondent No.3, filed Artha Rin Suit for realization of outstanding loan to the tune of Tk.5,22,07,752.98 but this defendant petitioners, making their appearance, filed written statement in order to contest the suit and also prayed to resolve the dispute by "settlement conference" under Section 21 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 but the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat rejected such prayer and considering the written statement as admission of a case stated in the plaint. The learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat has passed the impugned judgment and decree amounting to Tk.5,22,07,752.98 under Section 13 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and also directed to pay the interest in terms of the provision laid down in Section 50 of the said Ain, 2003. 

3. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the teamed Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners has brought to our notice that when defendant filed written statement with a prayer to resolve the dispute by way of "settlement conference" the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat to proceed with the matter in accordance with  the provision laid down in Section 21 of the said Ain, 2003 and there can be no scope to frame issue or to dispose of the suit under Section 13(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which is absolutely illegal and without any lawful authority. 

4. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners further submits that the recital of the written statement does not stand for admission of the claim of the plaintiff as required under Section 9(5) of the Artha Rin Adalaf Ain, 2003. Since in the instant case such an admission is lacking; the Court cannot invoke it's jurisdiction under Section 13(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in order to dispose of the matter in the manner, prescribed by law. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision of a caw Md. Arfan Uddin Akand & Others Vs. Artha Rin Adalat and others reported in 15 BLT (HCD) page 343 where their Lordships have clearly observed that since there is, no admission made in written statement as contemplated in Section 9(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the same cannot be brought within the mischief of Section 13(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The learned Advocate has - also referred another case of Mir Motiur Rahman Zihadi Vs. Artha Rin Adalat, Tangail and another reported in 15 BLT (AD) page 267. 

5. Mr. Ooswami has also argued that when the judgment and decree is found to have been passed without jurisdiction, the same can be challenged. 

6. On the other hand, Mr. M. Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2 submits that since the efficacious appellate forum under Section 41 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is available the judgment-debtor cannot be allowed to invoke the writ jurisdiction to agitate his grievances. Mr. Khaled further submits that if averment of the written statement clearly stands to admit the claim of the plaintiff and subsequently judgment-debtor is found to have agreed to pay the decneetal amount; the impugned judgment and decree passed under Section 13 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 cannot be disturbed merely on a technical ground. However, the judgment-debtor himself has agreed to re-pay the outstanding due in another writ petition. 

7. On the face of the submission, let as quote the relevant averment of the written statement where the defendant-judgment-debtor has invited to furnish the basic documents in order to give a better statement in subsequent occasion if it is so required.

“ক) ৰিবাদী প্রতিষ্ঠান কখনও' বাদী প্রতিষ্ঠানের নিকট হইতে কোন ঋণ গ্রহণ করে নাই, ঋনের আবেদন করে নাই বা কোন ঋণের বিপরীতে কোন চার্জ ডকুমেন্ট মৰ্টগেজ ডকুমেন্ট ইত্যাদি সম্পাদন করে নাই। তবে ইহা সত্য যে, বাদীর ব্যাংকের মাধ্যমে দেশ এবং বিদেশের বিভিন্ন প্রতিষ্ঠানের সাথে ব্যবসা করেছেন বাদী ব্যাংকে এলসি এবং ব্যাক টু ব্যাক মূলে রপ্তানীকৃত পণ্যের টাকা সংগ্রহ করেছেন এবং অনেক সময় লভ্যাংশের বিপরীতে জরুরী ভিত্তিতে ব্যাংকের সিসি এবং এসওডি হিসাবের মাধ্যমে টাকা উত্তোলন করেছেন ইহা সত্য তবে বাদী ব্যাংক এলসির বিপরীতে অনাদায়ী অংশের সমপরিমান বা তার চেয়ে কম উত্তোলন বা ওভার ড্রাফট মঞ্জুর করেছে এবং পরবর্তীতে এলসি টাকা আহরন করিয়া তাহা সমন্বয় করিয়াছে যে জন্য সিসি বা এসওডি হিসাবে কোন টাকা বাকী থাকার কারন নাই৷ বিত্ত বাদী ব্যাংকের কর্মচারী কর্মকর্তাগণ ভুল হিসাব প্রস্তুত করিয়া বাদী ব্যাংকেরে বিরুদ্ধে বর্তমান মামলা দায়ের করিয়াছেন৷"

The above statement, given by the defendant-petitioner, in the written statement certainly will not go to say that it is an admission as contemplated under Section 9(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which empowers the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat to invoke power under Section 13(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat has made the following observation in passing the impugned decree: 

“(খ)বিবাদী ব্যাংক বিবাদীগণের বরাবরে প্রেরিত সমনের সাথে আইনের বিধান মতে আরজির সমর্থনে দাখিলী কাগজাদি না দেওয়ায় বিবাদীগণ পূর্ণাঙ্গ জবাব দাখিল করিতে পারে নাই। পরবর্তীতে বাদী ব্যাংকের কাগজপত্র দাখিল হইলে বিবাদী অতিঃলিখিত জবাব দাখিলে অধিকার সংরক্ষন করনে।”

On the face of the decision it has become clear to us that there was an allegation against the maintainability of the suit for which Section 13 was not, at all, applicable. 

8. There is no doubt that the provision laid down in Section 13 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 has only empowered the learned Judge of the Court to dispose the matter but prior to invoke such jurisdiction the learned Judge is to comply other provisions laid down in Section 13(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Unfortunately relevant portion quoted from written statement cannot, at all, satisfy the Court to have a decision relating to the admission of the claim of the defendant-petitioner as contemplated in Section 9(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003. So the matter in issue is required to be adjudicated and determined with the help of document filed by the plaintiff including other evidence, adduced by the parties. 

9. It will not be out place to mention that rejection of the prayer filed by the defendant to dispose of the matter under Section 21 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 deserve no interference because in no circumstances the matter can be dissolved by A.D.R mechanism on the prayer of the defendant alone. It must be made by both the parties; otherwise it cannot be entertained by the learned Judge; hence the rejection of the prayer to resolve the dispute under Section 21 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 deserves no interference. Moreover, it is the Judge who is at liberty to dissolve the matter by settlement conference if both the parties so desire. 

10. However, considering the above facts and circumstances we are inclined to say that this case as has been made out does not come within the mischief of Section 130) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 and accordingly the decision taken by the Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat in order to dispose of the matter under Section 13(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is absolutely illegal of course, the learned Judge of the trial Court is to dispose of the matter in accordance with law within 60(sixty) days from the date of receipt of the order without allowing any party to drag the matter in their own manner. 

11. With these. observations this rule is made absolute in part so far it relates to dispose of the Artha Rin Suit under Section 130 ) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and so for it relates to rejection of the application under Section 21 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and decree made under Section 130) since is declared illegal and at the same time the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat is directed to dispose of the matter in accordance with the law and observation made above within 60 days positively. 

12. Let the judgment and order be sent to all concern for information and necessary action. 

End.

caseno:
Writ Petition No.7426 of 2011
With
Writ Petition 9407 of 2008
lawyer:
Mr. A. K. Mohammad Ali with Mrs. Fatema Begum, Advocates ------ For the petitioner in Writ Petition No.7426 of 2011 
Mr. Md. Humayun Kabir, Advocate ------ For the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 9407 of 2008 
Mrs. Ishrat Jahan with Mrs. Kashefa Hussain, Assistant Attorney Generals (with leave of the Court) ------ For the Government-respondents
parties:
Mrs. Shaheba Khatun ------ Petitioner in Writ Petition No. 7426 of 2011
Md. Ayub Ali ------ Petitioner in Writ Petition No. 9407 of 2008
Versus
Government of Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents in both the writ petitions
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Quddus. J:- These two writ petitions have been heard together, and are being disposed of by one judgment inasmuch as common questions of law and facts are involved in the cases. 

2. In both the Rules the writ petitioners, who are teachers of two different educational institutions, have sought for direction upon the respondents to pay their wear salaries. 

3. The petitioner in Writ Petition No.7426 of 2011 is an Assistant Teacher of Bamondanga Naser Mamud Di-Mukhi High School at Kurigram. On being appointed by a letter of appointment dated 08.03.2005, she joined the school on 10.03.2005 and her name was included in monthly pay order (in short MPO) with effect from September, 2006 against index No.1034095. Subsequently the Government portion of her salary was stopped from March, 2007 on a dispute with the Managing Committee of the School and her name was dropped from the MPO. Thereafter, the dispute was dissolved and her name was included in the MPO again from January, 2011. In spite of several representations and service of notice demanding justice upon the respondents, she did not get her arrear salary for the period of March, 2007 to December, 2010. 

4. The petitioner in Writ Petition No.9407 of 2008 joined Naldoani Abdus Salam Dakhil Madrasah at Dnmki Police Station under Patuakhali District as its Superintendent on 17.10.1994. During his service in the Madrasha, he was implicated in a criminal case for which the Managing Committee of the Madrasah by its resolution dated 22.04.2002 suspended him from service. During the period of suspension, he drew subsistence allowance i.e. 50% of salary. After being exonerated from the criminal case the Managing Committee of the Madrasah by its resolution dated 31.12.2003 reinstated him in service. After reinstatement he claimed his arrear salary i.e. the remaining 50%. In the meantime, he joined as Superintendent of Kalagachia Asmatia-Entazia Madrasah at Mirzagonj Police Station under Patuakhali District on 02.05.2004. However, the petitioner tiled an application dated 03.11.2008 to the Director General, Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (herein respondent No.2) requesting him to pay the remaining 50% of Government portion of his salary for the period of his suspension i.e. from 23.04.2002 to 31.12.2003, but without any result. 

5. Mr. A. K. Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate for the petitioner in Writ Petition No.7426 of 2011 submits that she has been continuously serving the school from her date of joining on 10.03.2005. The Head Master-incharge asked her not to attend the school and sign the attendants' book by an illegal order, challenging which she instituted a suit before a competent civil Court and obtained an order of temporary mandatory injunction on 07.10.2007. Subsequently the suit was decreed on compromise on 27.07.2010. In pursuance thereof, the petitioner has been getting her salary from January, 2011 though it was stopped from March, 2007. So it is her right to get the salary for the period of March, 2007 to December, 2010 and the respondents are bound to give it. 

6. Mr. Humayun Kabir, learned Advocate for the petitioner in Writ Petition No.9407 of 2008 submits that it has been decided in so many cases that after withdrawal of suspension order, the teachers of private school/madrasah, who were getting Government portion of their salary before suspension, will get arrear salary. With reference to annexure-E to the supplementary affidavit, he further submits that under similar circumstances respondent No.2 gave arrear salary to one Md. Delowar Hossain, Headmaster of Dogree Ismail Hossain High School, but discriminated against the petitioner in payment of his arrear salary. In support of his contention Mr. Kabir refers to the case of Md. Shahjahan Mia Vs. The Government of Bangladesh and others, 1 LNJ 547 and an unreported decision passed in Writ Petition No.3572 of 2010 (Md. Hafiz Uddin Vs. The Secretary, Ministry of Education and others)

7. Mrs. Ishrat Jahan, learned Assistant Attorney General opposes the Rules without filing any affidavit-in-opposition. She refers to clause 17 (3) of the বেসরকারী স্কুল/মাদ্রাসা শিক্ষক কর্মচারী বেতনের সরকারী অংশ ও জনবল কাঠামো-১৯৯৫, which provides no arrear salary or a part thereof to be paid to the teachers or employees of private school/madrasah, and submits that the respondents are not under any legal obligation to pay the arrear salary to the writ petitioners. Learned Assistant Attorney General further submits that in case of inaction on the part of the respondents or stopping payment, the petitioners could have approached the Government by preferring an appeal under clause 18 of the said guideline and in that count the writ petitions are not maintainable because of not exhausting the alternative remedy provided in the guideline, which is having the force of law. 

8. In turn of reply, Mr. Humayun Kabir submits that the remedy of appeal as provided in the guideline having not been published in official gazette and any procedure of filing the appeal having not been prescribed therein, it cannot be held to be an alternative remedy. On this point he refers to the case of Mongal Paita Perkhiddah College Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others, 15 BLT 481.

 9. The contentions of the writ petitioners are supported by some documents, which are annexed with their respective writ petitions and supplementary affidavits thereto, 

10. The petitioner in Writ Petition No.7426 of 2011 got her name included in the MPO from September, 2006 and accordingly she was getting Government portion of her salary, which was stopped from March, 2007. The Head Master-in-charge of the school by a letter dated 09.06.2007 asked her not to sign the attendants' book, which she challenged in Title Suit No.II9 of 2007 praying mandatory injunction to continue with payment of her salary. The Head Master-in-charge, Chairman of the Managing Committee and District Education Officer, Kurigram were made defendants therein. Ultimately the suit was decreed on compromise and a mandatory injunction was passed to that effect (vide annexure-F series to the supplementary affidavit affirmed on 19.06.2012). In compliance therewith, the petitioner started getting her salary from January, 2011. 

11. The suspension order against the petitioner in Writ Petition No.9407 of 2008 was withdrawn by the Managing Committee in its meeting held on 31.12.2003 (vide annexure-B to the writ petition) and he was exonerated from the criminal case by order dated 14.10.2004 (vide annexure-F to the supplementary affidavit affirmed on 11.10.2011). 

12. The notices of the Rules have been served upon all of the respondents, but no one has appeared to controvert the facts placed in the writ petitions or to challenge authenticity of the documents annexed thereto. 

13. In 15 BLT's case, under similar circumstances, the respondent's lawyer argued in same line that the petitioner failed to exhaust the provision of appeal. But the High Court Division held the writ petition maintainable relying on the case of Tafijul Islam Sarker Vs. Bangladesh and others, 3 BLC (AD) 135 and observed: 
"... In fact, in proper cases, the petitioner is entitled to file writ petition without exhausting the provision of appeal....an alternative remedy by way of appeal under a statue will not be a bar to a writ petitioner under article 102(2) of the Constitution if there is non-relaxable precondition for bringing the appeal. Moreover, the Nitimala, 1995 was not published in the Government gazette. Therefore, the Nitimala 1995 are for its internal administration of the Ministry of Education." 

14. In 1 LNJ, 547 and the unreported decision passed in Writ Petition No.3572 of 2010, two different Benches of the High Court Division under similar circumstances issued mandamus for releasing arrear salaries of the petitioner-teachers, who were suspended from service. We do not find any reason to differ with their lordships' view expressed in the said cases. 

15. Suspension from service is not a punishment and as such because of putting the petitioners on suspension, which did not culminate to any order of dismissal, they cannot be deprived of their salary.

16. In view of the discussions made above we find substance in the Rules and accordingly these are made absolute. The Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Education and the Director General, Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education, Dhaka (respondents No.1-2 in both the writ petitions) are directed to pay the arrear salaries and other benefits, if any to Shaheba Khatun, daughter of Md. Mojibur Rahman, Assistant Teacher of Bamandanga Nasr Mamud Di-Mukhi High School, Nageswari, Kurigram (petitioner in writ petition No.7426 of 2011) for the period, March, 2007 to December, 2010 and pay the remaining 50% of salary and other benefits, if any to Md. Ayub Ali, former Superintendent of Naldoani Abdus Salam Dakhil Madrasah, Police Station Dumki, Patuakhali (petitioner in writ petition No.9407 of 2008) for the period from 23.04.2002 to 31.12.2003 within 3 (three) months from the date of receipt of this judgment. 

17. Communicate the judgment. 

End.

caseno:
First Appeal No. 163 of 1992  
With
 Civil Rule No. 155(F) of 1992
lawyer:
Mr. Harun-Or-Rashid, Advocate ------  For the appellants
Mr. M. A. Mannan Mohan, Advocate ------ For the Respondent No. 1
Mr. Abul Kalam Mainuddin, Advocate  ------ For the Respondent No.2
parties:
Amal Kumar Chakrabarty being dead his heirs Debashish Chakrabarty and another ------  Defendant Appellants 
-Versus-
Md. Habibur Rahman and others ------ Plaintiff Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Sayed Mohammad Ziaul Karim, J.:-This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30.05.1992 passed by the learned Subordinate, First Court, Khulna in Title Suit No.41 of 1987 decreeing the suit. 

2. After filing of the appeal, a Rule was issued, calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 30.05.1992. should not be stayed. The Rule was registered as Civil Rule No.155(F) of 1992. Both the appeal and Rule having arisen out of a common judgment and decree, these have been heard together and are being disposed of by this judgment. 

3. Short facts leading to this appeal are that on 13.04.1987 the respondent Nos.1-2 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.41 of 1987 in the First Court Subordinate Judge, Khulna impleading appellants and respondent Nos.3-4 as defendants for Specific Performance of Contract to enforce an agreement of sale of 15 decimals land describes in the Schedule of the plaint. 

4. The plaintiff's case, put in a nutshell is that the property described in the Schedule of the plaint was originally belonged to Indra Sarker; that the plaintiffs were the tenants under him; that after the death of Indra Sarker defendant Nos.1-2 inherited the suit property and the plaintiffs were paying rent to them; that at the last part of 1980 defendant Nos.1-2 proposed to sale the suit property at a consideration of Tk.1,50,000/- and plaintiffs agreed to purchase the same, accordingly on different occasions plaintiffs paid Tk.50000/- to defendant Nos.1-2; that on 21.02.1982 defendant Nos.1-2 executed a baniapatra in favour of plaintiffs after receiving further Tk.90000/- and according to the terms of agreement defendant Nos.1-2 would execute and register sale deed after receiving rest Tk.10000/- and plaintiff would not pay rent; that the plaintiffs have .been possessing the suit property after renovation of the old building; that on repeated request the defendant Nos.1-2 failed to execute register sale deed after receiving Tk.10000/- and that on 20.12.1985, they lastly refused to execute sale deed. Hence the Suit. 

5. The defendant Nos.1-2 contested the suit by filling written statement denying all materials allegations made in the plaint and contending interalia that the plaintiffs were the tenants under them; that due to poverty, the plaintiffs became defaulter for payment of rent; that they served notice under section 106 of the Transfer Property Act for ejectmemnt of plaintiffs; that the plaintiffs created a baniapatra showing their forged signatures and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

6. On the pleading following issues were settled-
(a) Whether the suit was maintainable in the present from? 
(b) Whether the suit was barred by limitation? 
(c) Whether the plaintiff was entitled to get a decree as prayed for?
(d) Whether the deed of agreement was genuine? 
(e) To what relief, if any, the plaintiffs were entitled to? 

7. In course of trial the plaintiffs examined five witnesses, while contesting defendants examined one witness namely D.W.1 Amal Kumar Chakrabarty in support of their respective case. 

8. By the impugned decree the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Khulna decreed the suit. Hence the appeal. 

9. Mr. Harun Or Rashid, learned Advocate appearing for appellants supports the appeal and submits that the learned Judge of the trail Court ought to have considered the alleged agreement for sale of the suit land, was false, forged, fraudulent and without consideration and the appellants did not execute such agreement in favour of the plaintiffs and never received any consideration as alleged. He adds that having regard to the genuineness of the so-called agreement for sale the Court below miserably failed to take any consideration that the document had been sent to the hand writing expert for opinion at the instance of the plaintiffs but the expert did not pass any opinion, so it appears that the alleged agreement was not a genuine one and as such the same cannot be specifically enforced. The learned Counsel submits that the learned Judge of the court below failed to consider that the onus to prove the alleged agreement lies upon the plaintiffs. He adds that there is no evidence that the plaintiffs paid Tk.50000/- to defendant Nos.1-2 and it is absurd that plaintiffs paid Tk.140000/- out of 150000/-, so according to him the evidence of the plaintiffs in respect of material particulars suffer from glaring inconsistencies and contradictions and it is very unsafe to place reliance upon such evidence. The learned Counsel has drawn our attention to the order No.14 at page 36 of the Paper Book and submits that on 25.04.1992, the learned Judge of trail Court took specimen signatures of defendant Nos.l-2 at the instance of plaintiffs but without sending the same for expert opinion kept in the filed and himself compared the signatures which caused serious miscarriage of justice. In support of his contention he refers the case of Nurul Huq (Md) @ MN Huq Vs. Nirmal Chandra Dutta and another reported in 56 DLR (AD) 143 wherein it is held:  
"Code of Civil Procedure
Section 107 
In view of the parties contentions submissions of the it was the duty of the courts below to send the impugned documents to Handwriting Expert for opinion. Such opinion being not taken by either of the Courts below, the appeal is allowed, impugned judgment and decree are set aside. The first Appeal is remanded to the High Court Division with a direction to hear the appeal afresh after obtaining report from the competent Handwriting Expert as to execution of the documents." 

10. The learned Counsel further relied upon the case of Tarak Chandra Majhi Vs. Atahar Ali Howlader and others reported in 13 BLT (AD)-3 wherein it is held: 
"In case of contentious writing signature etc. though provision of section 73 of Evidence Act permits the court to compare the contentious signature with the admitted signature, the safe and best course in our view for the court would be to avoid the practice of comparing the writing or signature etc. and should not stake its judgment on the opinion formed or view taken upon resorting to risky or in other words unsatisfactory and dangerous procedure." 

11. The learned Counsel submits that suit is barred by limitation and he refers the case of Manindra Mohan Kar Vs. Ranadhir Dutta and others reported in 38 DLR (HC) 240 wherein it is held : 
"Limitation Act 
Article-113 
A suit for specific performance of contract has to be filed before expiry of 3 years of the date of notice of refusal as provided in Article 113 of the Limitation Act.
He adds that in this particular case the plaintiff could not prove his case particularly the alleged bainapatra. With this regard he refers the case of Md. Naimuddin Sarder Vs. Md. Abul Kalam Biswas and another reported in 39 DLR (AD)-237 wherein it is held: 
"Plaintiff in order to succeed must establish his own case to obtain a decree and weakness of defendants case is no ground for passing a decree in favour of the plaintiff." 
12. The learned Counsel submits that the appellant No.1 Amal Kumar Chakrabarty died on 03.10.1994 leaving behind Debasish Chakraborty as his only son, who on 30.04.1997 sold out .0750 acres land from the suit land to Md. Nurul Amin and Afroza Begum who are the son-in-law and daughter respectively of respondent No.1 Md. Habibur Rahman by a Kabala Deed dated 30.04.1997 and they purchased the suit land at the instance of respondent No.1 during the pendency of appeal, and as such by the alleged baina plaintiffs would not gain an advantage and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. 

13. The learned Counsel lastly submits that the learned Subordinate Judge failed to weigh and sift the evidence on record as required by law and evidently fell in an error in coming to his ultimate decision occasioning failure of justice. 

14. Mr. A.K. Mainuddin, learned Advocate appearing for respondent No.2 oppose the appeal and submits that on 21.02.1982 plaintiff and defendant Nos.1-2 entered into a valid agreement and on that day plaintiffs paid Tk.90000/- to them. He adds that on 20.12.1985 defendant Nos.1-2 refused to execute and register sale deed and on 13.04.1987 the plaintiffs filed the suit. So, the suit was field within time. The learned Counsel adds defendant No.2 Amal Kumar Chakrabarty is still alive but he was not examined by the plaintiff, so, he impliedly admitted his signature as genuine. He adds that the learned Judge of the trial Court himself compared the specimen signature of plaintiffs with that of the signatures in Baina and came to a conclusion that those signatures were not forged. 

15. In support of his contention the learned Counsel refers the case of Sk. Abul Qasam and others Vs. Mayez Uddin Modal and others reported in 45 DLR -169 wherein it is held : "Examination of L.T.I. -It is true Court itself can compare any signature or L.T.I. of any concerned person himself under section 73 Evidence Act but it is better to have an expert's opinion also, particularly in a case of L.T.I." 

16. He relied upon the case of Jahed Ali Mondal and others Vs. Jamini Kanta Dey and others reported in 1987 BLD (AD) 156 wherein it is held: 
"Onus -Onus on whom lies in a suit for specific performance of a contract for sale of property where the signatures in the documents recording the contract is admitted by the defendant pleading that the same were obtained from them by threat, intimidation and coercion law does not required that all facts alleged by the plaintiff shall be strictly proved, for burden of proof is often lightened by presumptions, admissions and estoppels -Primary onus of course lies, in a civil proceeding, upon the plaintiff -In this case primary onus has been discharged satisfactory by the plaintiff. Then onus has shifted upon the defendants to prove their particular fact that their signatures were extorted. This onus they failed to discharge. Consequently, the evidence adduced by the Plaintiffs as to the execution of the documents stands dismissed." 

He also refers the case of Aminun Nessa and others vs. Golam Kashem and others reported in 42 DLR 499 wherein it is held: 
"Burden of proof where initial onus is discharged by the plaintiffs by giving a slight evidence the burden shifts to the defendant to prove the contrary." 

17. The learned Counsel lastly submits that the plaintiffs .successfully proved their case by oral and documentary evidence and the impugned judgment and decree is just and proper which calls for on interference by this Court. 

18. Mr. M.A. Mannan, learned Advocate appearing for Respondent No.1 submits that in the meantime Debashish Chakrabarty son of late Amal Kumar Chakrabarty transferred .0750 acres of land to Md. Nurul Amin and Afroza Begum who are the son-in-law and daughter of respondent No.1 by a kabala deed dated 30.04.1997. 

19. In order to appreciate the submissions advanced by the learned Counsels of both sides, let us now weigh and sift the evidence on record adduced by both sides. 

20. P.W.1 Sheikh Sayed Ahmed was the scribe of bainapatra. He deposed that on 21.02.1982 he wrote bainapatra which he proved as Exht-1 and his signature there on as Exht-Ka. After completion of the bainapatra he handed over it to Amal Babu who and his brother perused the same. Thereafter Habibur Rahman gave Tk.90000/- to Komol Babu and they counted the same and admitted about taking of Tk.50000/-. Thereafter they singed in the bainapatra. He added that it was agreed that rest Taka 10000/- would be paid at the time of execution of sale deed. In cross examination he denied the suggestion that he was deposing falsely.

P.W.2 Habibur Rahman as plaintiff No.1 deposed that he was also deposing for plaintiff No.2. He added that they were the tenants under Indra Bhushan Chakrabarty in 15 decimals of land and they were paying rent regularly. Indra Bhushan Chakrabarty died within 1960-70; that after his death defendant Nos.1-2 proposed to sale the property at a consideration of TK.1500000/- prior to execution of bainapatra they paid Tk.50000/- as advance. He added that on 21.02.1982 he paid Tk.90,000/- to defendant Nos.1-2 and they executed baina. He added that Sheikh Sayed Ahmed (P.W.1) was the scribe of bainapatra and Md. Islam and Hafiz were the attesting witnesses of bainapatra, it was agreed that they would not pay rent further. He submits that within 1982-85 they expended Tk.50000/- for renovation of the old building. On many occasions he approached to defendant Nos.1-2 to execute the sale deed after taking rest Tk.10000/-. But lastly on 20.11.1985 they refused to do the same. Thereafter he filed the suit. In cross examination he stated that when defendant Nos.1-2 proposed to sale the property, no one was present there: He stated that the matter in dispute was locally placed in arbitration by 82 persons along with Abdul Jalil and Abdul Gani. He denied the suggestion that defendant Nos.1- 2 did not execute the bainapatra rather they forged their signatures. 

P.W3 Shah Mohammad Islam a local resident deposed that on 21-02-1982 the defendant Nos.1-2 executed a baina in his presence wherein he also singed as attesting witness and plaintiff No.1 paid Tk.90000/- to defendant Nos.1-2 in his presence. In cross examination he denied the suggestion that no bainapatra was written in his presence and as defendant No.1 lodged a criminal case against him and as such he was deposing falsely.

P.W.4 Shamsur Rahman deposed that on 21-02-1982 bainapatra Was written in his presence and Sayed Ahmed was the scribe. He added that Islam and Hafiz signed in the Bainapatra in his presence and it was agreed at the time of registration of deed rest money for Tk.10000/- would be paid.
P.W.5 A.H.M. Nur Ahmed deposed that plaintiff No.2 was his step sister. He stated that he used to help her. He added that a Criminal case was pending between the defendants and plaintiff No.1 and he had no knowledge about the transfer of the land. 

21. D.W.1 Amal Kumar Chakrabarty deposed that he was defendant No.1 and defendant No.2 was his younger brother. He also deposed on behalf of his brother. He added that the plaintiffs were the tenants under them since 1958. He added that for different causes the plaintiffs were suffering from poverty and they, with ulterior motive created a forged agreement in their names. The signatures as shown in the agreement were not their signature but the same were forged. He added that he never purchased the stamp for bainapatra and did not ask Sayed Ahmed to write any baina. The plaintiffs were defaulter for non payment of rent. He denied the suggestion that the consideration for the schedule property was fixed for Tk.1,50,000/- or he received Tk.50,000/- in different occasions or he further received Tk.90000/- or executed baina on 21-02-1982. In cross examination he stated that meanwhile he transferred some portion of the land to their tenants and he denied that he was deposing falsely. 

22. These are all of the material evidence adduced by both parties.

23. We have gone through the plaint, written statement, deposition of witnesses, all exhibits, other materials on record and given our anxious considerations to the submissions advanced by the learned Counsels of both sides. 

24. According to plaintiffs, defendant Nos. 1 -2 proposed to sale the Schedule Property at a consideration of Tk.150000/- and they agreed to purchase the same and accordingly they paid Tk.140000/- to defendant Nos.1-2 who on 21.02.1982 executed the bainapatra (Exht.1) in favour of them. On the contrary defendant Nos.1-2 disowned the plaintiff case as a whole and its case was that the bainapatra (Exht.1) was created showing their forged signatures. Now the question calls for consideration whether the baina (Exht.1) can be treated as valid contract and the same is specifically enforced. 

25. The point of determination whether the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Khulna was justified in passing the impugned judgment and decree. 

26. At the outset it will be profitable to extract section 12 of the Specific Relief Act which runs in the following manner:- 
"12. Cases in which specific performance enforceable-Except as otherwise provided in this Chapter, the specific performance of any contract may in the discretion of the Court be encored; 
(a) when the act agreed to be done is in the performance, wholly or partly, of a trust ; 
(b) when there exist no standard for ascertaining the actual damage caused by non-performance of the act agreed to be done ; 
(c) when the act agreed to be done is such that pecuniary compensation for its non-performance would not afford adequate relief ; or 
(d) when it is probable that pecuniary compensation cannot be got for the non-performance of the act agreed to be done. 

Explanation : Unless and until the contrary is proved, the Court shall presume that the breach of a contract to transfer immovable property cannot be adequately relieved by compensation in money, and that the breach of a contract to transfer moveable property can be thus relieved. 

27. Furthermore, Section 22 of the same Act provides that the Jurisdiction to decree specific performance is discretionary, and the Court is not bound to grant such relief merely because it is lawful to do so; but the discretion of the Court is not arbitrary but sound are reasonable guided by judicial principles and capable of correction by a Court of appeal.

28. On critical analysis of the evidence on record, we find that plaintiff No.1 was examined as P.W.2 and other witnesses were examined to corroborate him. PW.2 categorically narrated the plaint's case. He stated that when defendant Nos1-2 proposed to sale the schedule property at a consideration of Tk. I ,50,000/- then he and husband of plaintiff No.2 agreed to purchase the same and prior to execution of baina on different occasions he paid Tk.50,000/- to defendant Nos.1-2. Thereafter on 21.02.1982 defendant Nos.1 -2 executed baina in favour of them after receiving further Tk.90,000/-. His evidence regarding payment and execution of baina was corroborated by P.W.s 1, 3, 4 and 5. Although D.W. I denied his signature and the signature of his brother Komol Chakrabarty on baina but it is a matter of surprise that Komol Chakrabarty who was allegedly one of the executant did not come forward to deny his signature, without explanation. So the legal presumption would be had he been examined he would not have supported his brother's case. 

29. On close analysis of the evidence on record we find that the evidence of all these P.W.s in respect of payment and execution of baina dated 21.02.1982 (Exht. I) are consistent uniform and corroborated with each other, with all material particulars. There is absolutely no reason to disbelieve the consistent and corroborative evidence of those competent witnesses, having no reason whatsoever to depose falsely against the defendant Nos. 1-2. The defense extensively cross examined them but nothing could be elicited to shake their credibility in any manner whatsoever. So the same are invulnerable to the credibility. 

30. In a suit for Specific Performance of Contract, real question in such a suit whether there was a contract between the parties. We find that on 22-08-1989 the learned Judge of the trial Court took specimen signatures of defendant Nos.1-2 (Exht. Ka-Ka (24) and Kha-Kha (26) and compared the same with the signatures appeared in baina (Exht. l) and came to a definite conclusion that the baina (Exht. I) is not forged or fraudulent. We also closely scrutinized and compared the specimen signatures of defendant Nos.1 and 2 with that of the signatures shown in baina as well as Vokalatnama filed with the instant appeal and found that those are identical. 

31. It is well known that the evidence act has provided for the following four modes for proving hand-writing or signatures of a person in any document namely: - 
1. By the opinion of an expert who can examine and compare the handwriting or signatures in a scientific process vide Section 45 of the Evidence Act. 
2. By a witness who is acquainted with the hand-writing or signature of the person by whom the same is supposed to be written and singed vide Section 47 of the Evidence Act. 
3. By proof of the signature or hand-writing of the person alleged to have singed or written the document by evidence vide Section 67 of the Evidence Act. 
4. Also by comparison of the signature or handwriting of the person with his other admitted and proved handwriting or signature by the Court itself vide Section 73 of the Evidence Act. 
So, identity of the handwriting or signature of a person by the opinion of an expert is one of the method as provided in the Evidence Act. In the instant case when it is the duty of the plaintiffs to prove the identity and genuineness of the signatures of defendant Nos.1-2 on the alleged document, the plaintiffs may avail of any of the method as enumerated above. They cannot be forced by the defendants to resort to any particular method of proving the alleged signature. With this regard reliance is being placed in the case of Sree Dulal Baneijee@ Moni Vs. Sree Sharat Chandra Pal and another reported in 12 BLD 277. 

32. We, therefore, hold that the baina (Exht.1) executed by defendant Nos.1-2 in favour of plaintiff is genuine and specific performance of contract be enforced. The impugned judgment and decree passed by the trial Court are well reasoned backed by sufficient oral and documentary evidence and all the issues involved in the suit have rightly been settled, considered and decided by trial Court with reference to the evidence and materials on record, which cannot be interfered. 

33. We have gone through the facts of the cases as refereed by the learned Counsel for the plaintiffs, we are in respectful agreement 4 with the principles enunciated in those cases, but the facts leading to those cases are distinguishable with that of the instant case and as such we are unable to accept the submissions advanced by the learned Counsel for the appellants, on the contrary the legal plea taken by the learned Counsel for the respondent No.2 prevails and appears to have a good deal of force. 

34. Having considered the facts and. circumstances of the case and forging narrative, we lead to the conclusion that the impugned judgment and decree suffer from no illegality and impropriety which calls for no interference by this Court thus the appeal having no merit fails. 

35. In the result, the appeal is dismissed with cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 30.05.1992 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Khulna in Title Suit No.41 of 1987 is hereby affirmed. The Civil Rule No. 155(F) of 1992 also having no merit fails and is discharged with the observation made above. 

36. Send down the lower Court's record at once. 

End.

parties:
Enayetullah and others ----- Defendant-Appellant-Petitioners
Versus
Arfuza Begum being dead her heirs-l(a) Abul Kashem and others ----- Plaintiff-Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1-6 to show cause as to why the judgment and order of affordance dated 22.042004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge. Bhola in Miscellaneous Appeal No.31 of 1994 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the predecessor of the present opposite party No.1-6 one Faizunnessa as plaintiff tiled the original Title Suit No.49 of 1987 in the court of the then Sub-ordinate Judge. Bhola against the present petitioners for partition. The plaintiffs on 25.08.1987 filed an application under Order 39, Rule I read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for an order of temporary injunction against the defendants. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge after hearing the said application passed an order of status-quo on 25.08.1987 directing the parties to maintain status-quo with a notice to show cause upon the defendants as to why the temporary injunction should not be granted. The present petitioner No.1 on 09.09.1987 received the said notice and accordingly submitted written objection. The order of status-quo was not extended further and eventually the application for temporary injunction was not heard. On 30.01.1988 the plaintiff filed an application under Order 39, Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure upon which a Miscellaneous case being No.7 of 1988 was started. In the said Miscellaneous case the plaintiff alleged that during pendency of the order of status-quo the present petitioners along with others on 21.01.1988 forcibly entered into the schedule land and made obstruction in cultivation and also damaged the standing crops ("Mugdal") of 128 decimals of land causing damage of Tk.5,000/-. The plaintiff also lodged a G.D. entry in the respective Police Station and the Police authority served notice under section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure but ultimately all are in vain. The present petitioners after getting notice of the violation Miscellaneous case filed written objection and denied all the allegations raised against them contending inter-alia that the statement made in the application under order 39, Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure is false, fabricated and the defendant-petitioners never violated the order of status-quo. The original Title Suit No.49 of 1987 was decreed on 04.11.1993 and being aggrieved the defendants preferred Title Appeal No.47 of 1994 in the court of learned District Judge, Bhola which was admitted for hearing by the said court and the learned District Judge called for the lower court's record and transmitted the case to the court of learned Subordinate Judge. The learned Advocate for the defendants talked to the defendants that the hearing of the violation miscellaneous case might not be held by the court and accordingly no step was taken by the defendants who are the opposite parties to the violation miscellaneous case. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Bhola on 02.07.1994 behind the back of the present petitioners after examining one witness passed an ex-parte judgment and order of conviction of six months civil imprisonment. 

3. Being aggrieved the present petitioners as appellants preferred a Miscellaneous Appeal No.31 of 1994 in the court of learned District Judge, Bhola which was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, Bhola and the learned lower appellate court by the impugned judgment and order dated 22.04.2004 dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and order of the learned Subordinate Judge. 

4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order the defendant-appellant-petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay. 

5. Mr. Abdul Jalil, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite party No.2 and 4-6. 

6. The learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during passing the judgment and order committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the ad-interim order of status-quo was passed on 25.08.1987 and the application for injunction was filed on 21.08.1987. In fact on 21.08.1987 there was no order of status-quo against the petitioners. The trial court passed an order of civil imprisonment on 02.07.1994 but the fact remains that on the date of alleged violation of the order of status-quo there was no order of status-quo or injunction whatsoever against the present petitioners. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge is totally misconceived in this regard and by non-application of mind he passed the ex-parte order on 02.07.1994 and subsequently the lower appellate court without entering into the facts of the case being guided by surmise and conjecture upheld the order of the trial court by the impugned judgment and order dated 22.04.2004. The learned Advocate also submits that the trial court was without jurisdiction to pass any order on 02.07.1994 inasmuch as against the judgment and decree of the original Title Suit 49 of 1987 a Title Appeal was pending wherein the original record was called for and the order was communicated to the court of learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Bhola. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the violation Miscellaneous case since is quasi criminal in nature the trial court had incumbent duty to bring charge in the form of issues mentioning the date of occurrence, time of occurrence and manner of occurrence and in this context the learned counsel referred some decisions of this court reported in 12 BLD 544, 39 DLR 262, 1987 BLD 73, 13 BLD 532. 
7. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court committed no illegality in passing the order of civil imprisonment and the order of affordance respectively. The learned Advocate further submits that on 25.08.1987 the learned trial court in Title Suit No.49 of 1987 passed an order of status-quo and after that order following date was fixed on 20.09.1987 and had there been no such extension order of status-quo, the learned courts below might not have been passed the order of imprisonment. The learned Advocate also submits that the written objection which was filed in the violation Miscellaneous case does not disclose that on 21.01.1988 there was no order of status-quo_ or injunction against the defendants. The learned Advocate lastly submits that both the courts below after perusal of the connected papers and deposition of the petitioner No. I (ka) of the violation Miscellaneous case No.7 of 1988 being satisfied passed the order which is lawful and is not liable to be interfered with. 

8. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the case records, connected papers, deposition of the witness Md. Hanif Mia and the concerned application for violation of the courts order along with the written objection filed against that. 

9. On perusal of the case records it transpires that the plaintiff to the suit on 20.08.1987 filed an application for temporary injunction against the defendants of the original partition suit being No.49 of 1987. On that application the learned trial court passed an order of status-quo vide order No.4 on 25.08,1987 until) the reply of show cause notice from the side of the defendants. The defendants subsequently appeared after getting show cause notice and submitted written objection. The allegation of violation was raised on the date of occurrence i.e. on 21.01.1988 but prior to that the defendants submitted their written objection. No where it is noticed that the ad-interim order of status-quo was extended after 25.08.1987. The petitioner 1(ka) of the violation Miscellaneous case No.7 of 1988 in his testimony admits that after service of notice the defendants appeared and submitted written objection. Subsequent to that on 21.01.1988 violating the order of status-quo they have damaged the crops valued Tk.5,000/-. The learned lower appellate court without entering into the case record relied upon the Miscellaneous petition and the order of civil imprisonment which was passed ex-parte by the learned trial court vide order No.153 dated 02.07.1994,

10. In a case or proceedings for violation of injunction it is the incumbent duty upon the court to bring charge in the form of points for determination disclosing all material particulars of the allegation i.e. the date of occurrence, time of occurrence and manner of occurrence since the case is of quasi criminal in nature. The proposition of law has imposed a mandatory duty upon the trial court to dispose of the matter in accordance with the direction but apparently the learned trial court passed an order of civil imprisonment without compliance of that, which is evasive in nature and not speaking and well reasoned. The learned appellate court subsequently ignoring the provisions of law and facts of the case affirmed the order of the trial court illegally which deserve interference of this court. 

11. In the result, the Rule having much substance is made absolute without any order as to costs. The judgment and order of affirmance dated 22.04.2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Bhola in Miscellaneous Appeal No.31 of 1994 is hereby set aside. 

12. The order of stay granted earlier by this court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated. 

13. Let a copy of this judgment along with the lower court's record be sent down at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Prabir Neogi, Adv. ------- For the petitioners 
Mr. Gopal Chandra Saha, A.A.G. with Mrs. Suchorita Sen Gupta, A.A.G. ------- For the Opposite Parties

Vs
