full_judgment:
Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal .J:- This. Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 2.38.2010 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Court, Gazipur in Title Appeal. No.34 of 2010 affirming those dated 24.11.2009 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 100 of 2009 should not be seaside.

2. Material facts of the case in brief are that the opposite party No.1. Barbara Rosario as plaintiff brought the aforesaid Title Suit No.100 of 2009 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Gazipur for cancellation of the gift Deed No2453 dated 30.6.2(0)4 registered in. Tongi Sub-registry Office in respect of the suit land as described in the schedule of the plaint on the averments that the C.S. recorded tenant of the suit land as described in the schedule of the plaint was Razu Rosario, who died leaving behind only son Gabriel Rosario alias Cahn Rosario whose name has been rightly recorded in S.A. 181 and R. S. Khatian Nos.92 and 93. Gabriel. Rosario died leaving behind 3 sons and 3 daughters as his legal heirs and the plaintiff got 31.25 decimals of land including the :suit land on amicable partition. The plaintiffs husband died leaving behind the plaintiff and two children, the plaintiff being earned the livelihood by working in small NGO. In this backdrop the defendant Nos. 1-2 in the first part of the year 2003 told the plaintiff that they have good relation with the Manager and other officials of the House Building Finance Corporation and thus, they can mintage to get loan of Tk. 10/15 Lac from the House Building Finance Corporation. The plaintiff then being a helpless widow believed the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in good faith and gave the Photostat copies of the relevant papers and Tk.20,000/- to the defendant No. 1. After 3/4 months later the defendant No. 1 told that loan amount of I0,00,000/- has been sanctioned and claimed some additional costs. The plaintiff, thereupon, lending some money gave Tk.30, 000/-to the defendant No.1 as costs and the defendant Nos. l and 2 took signature of the plaintiff on blank stamps. After 10/15 days while the plaintiff asked the defendant nos. 1-2 about the loan then the defendant No.1 told that the plaintiff will get loan amount within 4/5 days but after 5 days defendant No.1 told that it will take some more time. The plaintiff, thereafter; disclosed the matter to her relatives and ultimately, the defendant No. 1 on 12.10.2003 denied the whole matter. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 thereafter, on 28.3.2006 threatened the plaintiff stating that they will dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land and claimed the suit land on the basis of the impugned deed. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 created the gift deed collusively in order to grab the suit land. The plaintiff never went to the Sub-registry office to execute and register the impugned deed and hence, the suit.

3. The petitioner (defendant No.1) and defendant No.2 entered appearance in the suit and filed written statement denying most of allegations of the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner inasmuch as the suit is barred by estoppel, waiver and acquiescence. The plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 voluntarily gifted the suit land in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 (nephews of the plaintiff) and registered the impugned deed of gift No.2453 dated 30-6-2004 AD and on the same day delivered possession of the suit land to Mein and since then the defendants have been residing thereon by mutating their name and paying rents to the Government. The plaintiff has no right, title and interest in the suit land and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned Assistant Judge, upon considering the pleadings of the parties framed the following issues for determination:-

(i) Whether the suit is maintainable in its present form?

(ii) Whether the suit is barred by limitation?

(iii) Whether the impugned gift No.2453 dated 30.6.2004 is liable be cancelled'?

(iv) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree, as prayed for or any other reliefs?

5. At the trial plaintiff side examined as many as 3 witnesses and the defendant side examined 2 witnesses and both the parties also exhibited some documents including gift deed No.2453 dated 30.6.2004 and hand writing expert's opinion.

6. The learned Assistant Judge upon hearing argument of the parties and on considering the materials on record by his judgment and decree dated 24.11.2009 decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff. Against which the defendant Nos. 1 -4 preferred Title Appeal No. 34 of 2010 in the Court of District Judge, Gazipur which was eventually, transmitted to the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur for disposal, who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 23.8.2010 affirmed the decision of the trail Court on the finding that the trial Court rightly on assigning sound reason doubted the execution of deed of gift dated 30.6.2004.

7. Being aggrieved thereby the present defendant- petitioner has come before this and obtained the present Rule.

8. Mr. Khandker Aminul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-appellant-petitioner, Bimol Rosario submits that both the Courts below without applying its judicial mind into the facts and circumstance of the case and law bearing on the subject most illegally disbelieved the execution of the registered deed of gift dated 30.6.2004 (Ext. A) and the same has occasioned failure of justice. He next upon placing Ext. B, hand writing expert's opinion submits that DW-2, hand writing expert upon applying modern technology found signatures of the plaintiff appearing in the deed of gift in question are not forged and hand writing expert as DV9-2 in his deposition categorically stated that the deed of gift is genuine and he proved his investigation report along with films as "Ext. B series" though, both the Courts below without assigning any sound reason rejected the report submitted by DW-2. Mr. Khandker Aminul Haque, the learned Advocate while elaborating his submission referred to the decisions reported in 19 BLT 05 and 19 BLT 568 and submits that in this modern world science has been developing day by day and it is also need of the day to detect the truth by applying modern technology and it is apparent from the record that in this case the officer of the CID in order to detect the genuineness of thumb impression of the plaintiff-opposite party by applying modem technology has found that the thumb impressions on the alleged documents with the admitted thumb impressions of the plaintiff are in the hand of the plaintiff-opposite party and in that view of the matter both the Courts below ought to have believed the report of the hand writing expert and in not doing so committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice.

9. Mr. Moudud Ahmed. the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party No.1, on the other hand, by filing counter affidavit contested the Rule. Mr. Moudud Ahmed in the course Of his argument upon placing the judgments of two Courts below submits that both The Courts below on perusing the deed in question (Ext.1) found there is overwriting, re-writing, wrong spelling in the signatures of the donor and DW-2 in his cross-examination admitted that date of the impugned deed and the date in the thumb impression book is not the same and in that view of the matter both the Courts below rightly ignored the expert's opinion. Mr. Moudud Ahmed further points out that at the trial the defendants miserably failed to examine any witness to prove their so-called deed of gift which raised a serious question of doubt as to the genuineness of the deed of gift and in that view of the matter both the Courts below committed. no wrong in canceling the impugned gift deed No.2453 dated 30.6.2004 AD registered at Tongi Sub-registry office. Finally, Mr. Moudud Ahmed contends that in the facts and Circumstance of the case with regard to probability and improbability the learned Judge of the Court of appeal below rightly held "that the plaintiff is a 45 years old lady, she has two minor children. It is quite unnatural that depriving than minor child their mother could gift her property to her nephews."

10. Mr. Moudud Ahmed in support of his submission has relied on the decisions reported in 37 DLR (AD) 205. 45 DLR 279 and 19 DLR 188

11. I have beard the learned Advocates of both the sides at length and perused the Revision application, judgments of two COLMS below, deposition of witnesses, exhibits and other materials on record.

12. Now the fear question for consideration in this case whether both the Courts below were justified in canceling the deed of Helm (Ext. A) upon disbelieving expert's opinion (Ext. B series).

13. As I have already noticed that the opposite patty No. l as plaintiff filed Title Suit No 100 of 2009 in the Court of Assistant Judge. 3rd Court. Gazipur for cancellation of the gift deed No.2453 dared 30.6 2004 registered at Tongi Sub-registry office as describer' in the schedule of the plaint. It is found that the plaintiff-opposite-party to prove his case examined 3 witnesses and the plaintiff herself was examined as PW-1, who in her deposition Stated that:-  “নাঃ জমিতে আমি ভোগ দখলে থাকাকালে স্বামী মারা যায়। ১ পুত্র ও কন্যা রেখে। ১/২ নং বিবাদী আমাকে ব্যাংকের থেকে লোন নিয়ে দিবে বলে জানায়। সে জমিতে বিল্ডিং করে বাস করার জন্য। এজন্য কিছু টাকা সহ জমির কাগজপত্র দিই। কিন্তু লোন নাই। বলে যে ব্যাংকের সংগে চুক্তি করা লাগবে, ষ্ট্যাম্পে সই লাগবে। আমি ৫টি ষ্ট্যাম্পে সই দিই্। ষ্ট্যাম ও টাকা ফেরত চাই। ১/২৩ নং বিবাদী বলে যে, টাকাও নাই, জমিও নাই্ আত্মীয় স্বজনকে জানাই। তল্লাশী দিয়ে নাঃ জাঃ দলিলের নকল উঠিয়ে বিগত ৪/৯/২০০৬ ইং তাং নাঃ জাঃ দলিলের বিষয় জানতে পারি। ২৪৫৩ নং দানপত্র দলিল ৩০/৬/২০০৪ ইং তাং আমি কখনো রেজিষ্ট্রি করে দেই নাই্।”

14. PW-2, Malati Rosario stated in her deposition that the plaintiff is her sister and the defendants are her nephews and her sister got the suit land by inheritance. This witness also stated that she came to know about the forged deed from the plaintiff. This witness in her cross-examination denied the suggestion that she deposed falsely as per instruction of her sister.

15. PW 3, Somor Rosario, who stated in his position that:-

আমি বাদী বিবাদী নাঃ জমি চিনি। বাদী আমার পিসী। বিবাদীরা চাচাতো ভাই । বিবাদীরা লোন দেবার কথা বলে নাঃ জমির দলিল করে নেয়। নাঃ জমি বাদী শাক সবজি করে ভোগ করেন।

16. Let me now advert to the evidence of defendant side. It appears that defendant No. 1 Bimol Rosario himself was examined as DW-1, who in his deposition stated that:-

বাদীসহ আমার অন্যান্য ফুপুগনের সংগে খুব ভাল সম্পর্ক, বড়দিন, ইষ্টার সানডে সহ বিতিনন পালা শুর পাঠনে আমাদের বাড়ীতে আসতেন। আমরা আদর আপ্যায়ন করতাম। বাদী উক্তরুপে আমাদের প্রতি সন্তষ্ট হয়ে নাঃ সম্পত্তি দান ���রে দখল বুঝিয়ে দেন।

17. DW-2, Shahidullah, who examined the thumb impressions of the plaintiff as hand writing expert kind submitted a report. This witness proved, his report along with films as "Ext. B series". This witness in his cross-examination also stated that “প্রতিবেদনে কি প্রকারের ছাপ করেছি তা উল্লেখ করি নাই। জানতে চায় নাই।”

18. It is found that the trial Court below oil consideration of the evidencial materials on record canto to a finding that "DW-2 admitted that date of the impugned used and the date in thumb impression book, is not the same even what type of impress on has been examined is not mentioned in the report." On perusal of the exhibits and the depositions of the DWs. contradicts found and as such the expert opinion is rejected and on this 'finding the learned Assistant Judge cancelled the deed in question (Ext. A) and decreed the suit. Furter, it appears from the "Ext. A" that the attesting witness of the impugned deed was not the member of the donee and donar's DW-1 in his cross-examination admitted that:- “নাঃ দলিলে আমার অন্য কোন পিসাতো ভাই সাক্ষী নাই। নাঃ দলিলের সাক্ষী একজন আমার প্রতিবেশী অপর জন আমার শ্বশুর।”

19. In this case it is found that the defendant Nos. 1-2 did not or could not examine any attesting witness to prove the deed of gift (Ext. A). It is also found that the appellate Court below on the facts of the case and on consideration of the evidence and materials on record arrived at a finding that "the plaintiff is a 45 years old lady, she has two minor children. It is quite unnatural that depriving that minor child their mother could gift her property to her nephews."

20. On a close perusal of the record. I find nothing on record to suggest that any of the witnesses corroborated the evidence of DW-1 on the point of possession of the defendant-petitioner in the suit land.

<u>21. The proposition of law is by now well settled that the expert's opinion is not a conclusive evidence which enables the Court to come to a satisfactory conclusion though the said opinion is not binding upon the Court. The Court itself can compare any signature or LTI of any concerned person under section 73 of the Evidence Act and come to or decision in accordance with law.</u>

22. In this ease the trial Court as well as the Court of appeal below considered the entire  evidence on record and come to a concurrent finding that in the facts and circumstances of the case there was no reason on the part of the plaintiff-opposite party to gift the suit land, to her nephews depriving her minor child.

23. On assessment of the evidence on record together with the impugned deed of gift dated 30.6.2004 (Ext. A), I do not find any valid ground to differ with the view taken by the Courts below. Therefore, I am unable to accept the contentions raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that both the Courts below without applying its judicial mind into the facts and circumstance of the case most illegally rejected the expert's opinion and decreed the suit.

24. The decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner are distinguishable on facts.

25. In view of try discussion made in the foregoing paragraphs it is by now clear dint the instant Rule must fail.

26. In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The judgments of both the Courts below are hereby maintained.

27. Let a copy of this judgment along with the lower Courts record he sent down at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, J :- The defendant petitioner obtained Rule upon making a revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure against an order dated 25.07.2000 passed by the Assistant Judge, Mirpur, Kustia in title suit No.133 of 1997 which rejected the prayer for Local inspection. 

2. That the case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Sibram Agorwala who died leaving son Gobinda Lal Agorwala. Gobinda Agorwala left this country just after partition of India and he died there. Gobinda Lal Agorwala was non-Bengali as such the suit land became the vested property. S.A. record was prepared in the name of Gobinda Lal Agorwala in S.A. Khatian No.405 and the plaintiff possessed the suit land through lease. The defendant took settlement as khas land and that settlement was cancelled on 30.10.85. During R.S. operation, suit land was recorded in the name of defendant Nos. 1 to 3 and on 7.5.97 the defendant threatened to dispossess. Hence the plaintiffs filed the suit. 

3. The defendants No.1 to 3 appeared and contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable and the suit is barred by law of limitation. The suit land belonged to Sibram Agorwala who surrendered to the landlord to Satish Chandra Basu Mollik and subsequently the suit land became the khas land of the Government.

4. It is further stated that the suit land settled to defendant Nos.1 and 2 by settlement case No. 5/13/75-76 and to the defendant No.3 in settlement case No. 2/13/75-76 who possessed the same and subsequently the Government decided to give long term settlement and thus the Government executed a deed in favour of defendants on 17.08.80. After lease the defendants Nos. 1 to 3 constructed 3 pucca godown on the suit land and they carried on business peacefully. During R.S. operation, R.S. record was preliminary recorded in the names of defendants Nos.1 to 3. Thereafter the Government filed objection Case No.217 that was rejected and R.S. record was finally published in the name of defendants Nos.1 to 3. The defendant Nos.1 to 3 paid rent to the Government upto 1405 B.S. The plaintiff have/had no right, title and possession in the suit land. Hence the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

5. On 18.07.2000 the Tahasilder of Mirpur Land Office was examined as P.W. 2 who stated in his evidence that- 
“ নালিশী জমির উপর কিছু ফাঁকা জায়গা আছে। সেখানে ৪নং বিবাদী ইটের ব্যবসা করে। কিছু জমিতে গুদাম ঘর আছে। উক্ত গুদাম ঘর গুলির সাবেক মালিকগনের এবং পরিত্যাক্ত সত্য নয় যে, উক্ত গুদাম ঘরগুলি নতুন”।

6. On 25.07.2000 the defendant Nos. l to 3 filed an application for local inspection. On 25.7.2000 the learned trial court heard the application and rejected the same by his judgment and order No.37 dated 25.07.2000 without giving any reason. 

7. Being aggrieved by the order No.37 dated 25.07.2000, the defendant petitioners preferred the instant Civil Revision under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure before this Division and obtained the present Rule. 
8. Mr. Saidul Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appeared for petitioner and Mr. Md. Ali Jinnah, the learned Assistant Attorney General appeared for the State-Opposite party. 

9. Heard the learned Advocates for both sides perused the revisional application, application for local inspection filed under order XXVI Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure on behalf of defendant Nos.1-3, impugned order passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mirpur, Kustia. No written objection against the application for local inspection was filed by the plaintiffs. 

10. In the application under Order XXVI Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure the defendants prayed for local inspection on three points namely:
১। নালিশী জমিতে পুরাতন পরিত্যক্ত গৃহাদি বিদ্যমান আছে কি না?
২। নালিশী জমিতে ৩টা গোডাউন ঘর আছে কিনা?
তাহার আনুমানিক বয়স কত বছর?
৩। নালিশী জমিতে কোন ইটের ব্যবসা চালু আছে কি না?

The learned Trial Court on perusal of the application for local inspection and on hearing the submission of the learned Advocate for defendant petitioners rejected the same by his impugned order no.37 dated 25.07.2000 on flimsy ground simply on the ground that the defendant did not pray local inspection earlier as such the application for local inspection is not considered at this belated stage as the suit is in the final stage. 

11. Mr. Saidul Alam Khan the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that no where in their plaint stated that they possessed the suit land, so the defendants are not required to pray for local inspection before evidence as such the Trial Court committed serious error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

 12. That the learned Advocate petitioners further submits stated in his evidence that — “ নালিশী জমির উপর কিছু ফাঁকা জায়গা আছে। সেখানে ৪নং বিবাদী ইটের ব্যবসা করে। কিছু জমিতে গুদাম ঘর আছে। উক্ত গুদাম ঘর গুলির সাবেক মালিকগনের এবং পরিত্যক্ত সত্য নয় যে, উক্ত গুদাম ঘরগুলি নতুন”।
In this context, he submits that it is not the case of the plaintiffs. On the other hand, the defendant's case is that there is no brick on the suit land and the godown is not at all old as such it is just and covenant to determine the real controversy between the parties by way of local inspection in such view of the matter the trial court committed serious error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in rejecting the application for local inspection. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that without local inspection only by adducing oral evidence it is not at all possible to arrive at a correct finding over the matter in dispute. So in order to find out the real controversy between the parties, the application under Order XXVI Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure ought to have considered by the learned Assistant Judge, Mirpur, Kushtia on merit and non-consideration of the application for local inspection by the learned Assistant Judge, Mirpur, Kushtia has caused a serious miscarriage of justice which has resulted an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. It is further stated that the impugned order passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mirpur, Kushtia is totally misconceived one and .the same is also a non-speaking order as such the same deserves interference under the provision of law as contain in section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

13. The learned Advocate in course of his submission draws my attention to the impugned order passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mirpur, Kushtia is totally a non-speaking order which I also find force in the said submission of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and as such the impugned order of the learned Assistant Judge, Mirpur, Kushtia is not tenable in the eye of law and as such the same deserves interference under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure in view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case the impugned judgment and order of the learned Assistant Judge, 'Mirpur, Kushtia is liable to be set aside.

14. The petitioner refers the case of Abdus Sattar (Md) and others Vs. Lalon Mazar Sharif and Seba Sadan Committee and others reported in 56 DLR (AD) Page 180. In that decision it is clearly held that the report itself of the Advocate Commissioner is not evidence but if the Commissioner deposes on oath before the court then the same is evidence. The learned Advocate for the petitioner next refers the case of Sree Ratan Chandra Deb Gupta Vs Comilla Pourashava reported in 12 B.L.T (HCD) page 290 where in their Lordships held that there is no bar for the appellate court to exercise the jurisdiction under order XXVI, Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the facts of a case. Such step is definitely taken, as an aid of the final decision that may be arrived at in the appeal. The learned court before passing the impugned order did not at all take into consideration that in order learned Advocate for the in course of his submission XXVI Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure it is clearly mentioned that in any suit in which the court deems a local O. inspection to be requisite or proper for the purpose of elucidating any matter in dispute, or of ascertaining the market-value of any property, or the amount or any mesne profits or damages or annual net profits, the Court may issue a commission to such person as it thinks fit directing him to make such inspection and to report thereon to the Court. The Trial Court before 'passing the impugned order ought to have taken into consideration this vital provision of law as contained in Order XXVI Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure without taking into consideration of the relevant provision of law, the learned Trial Court-arrived at an erroneous finding in rejecting the application under Order XXVI Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the impugned order as passed by the learned Trial Court on the application for local inspection suffers from gross illegality and material irregularity. As such the 14 impugned order of the learned Assistant Judge, Mirpur, Kustia passed in Title Suit No.133 of 1997 in rejecting the application for local inspection is not sustainable in law and the same is liable to be set aside. 

15. On the other hand Mr. Md. Ali Jinnah, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the State  Opposite party frankly concedes that the impugned order is a non-speaking order so in view of the submissions as advanced by the learned 40 Advocate for the petitioners and the decisions reported in 56 DLR (AD) 180 and in 12 BLT (HCD) 290 of our Apex Court I am of the view that the impugned order of the learned Assistant Judge Mirpur, Kustia passed in Title suit No.133 of 1997 suffers from serious miscarriage of Justice which has resulted an error in the decision occasioning in failure of Justice. I find, substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.  
The impugned Order No.37 dated 25.07.2000 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mirpur, Kustia in Title Suit No.133 of 1997 is hereby set aside. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hearby recalled and vacated. The learned Trial Court is hereby directed to dispose of the application under Order XXVI Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure on merit giving opportunity to both sides and dispose of the same preferably within 2 (two) months and the learned Advocate Commissioner if so appointed by the learned Trial Court is hereby directed to submit his report within 1(one) month. 

16. Since it is a very old case the learned trial Court is hereby directed to conclude the trial of the suit preferably within 2(two) months from the date of submission of the report by the learned Advocate Commissioner. 

17. Send down the L.C.R. along with a copy of this judgment to the concerned court at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Rezaul Hasan, J:- In this petition filed by the petitioner under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-4 to show as to why the judgment and decree dated 03.02.2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No.69 of 2011, reversing those dated 20.06.2011 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Matlab, Chandpur in Title Suit No.62 of 2011 should not be set aside and / or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. It has been stated in the plaint, amongst other, that the petitioner as plaintiff filed on 13.03.2008, Title Suit No.62 of 2011 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Matlab, Chandpur for declaration that the 'Kha' schedule document dated 17.02.2008 in respect of `Ka' schedule land is collusive, fraudulent, without consideration, inoperative, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs; that according to the testimonial, given by the school, the date of birth of the plaintiff is 04.06.1992; that he was less than 16 years age and was a minor; that the defendants fixed the consideration for the suit land at Tk.1,60,000.00 (one lac sixty thousand) and the Plaintiff having been induced agree to sell the land and on 17.02.2008 the defendants took the plaintiff to the Sub-registrar office and in collusion with the scribe and the witnesses managed  get the impugned document executed and registered in their favour, that the defendants only gave 14,000/- taka to the plaintiff with  false assurance of giving the rest of the  money within a short time and after registration, that the defendants detained plaintiff for 5 days and after having such knowledge the mother of the plaintiff filed G.R. Case No. 18 of 2008 on 20.02.2008 and the police rescued the plaintiff from the custody of the defendant No.2; that there was no transfer with the free consent and no consideration was paid to the plaintiff and the plaintiff had no legal capacity to execute or register the disputed document. Hence, the suit. (Underlining is mine) 

3. The defendant Nos.1-4 filed written statements denying all material allegations averred in the plaint and further contending, inter alia, that the plaintiff was the owner and was in possession of the suit land acquired by inheritance. After death of his father he lived in his paternal house, while his mother lived in Dhaka. Plaintiff had pressed for money to go abroad and proposed the defendant Nos.1-4 to sell the suit land. Earlier the plaintiff offered his uncles to buy the suit property, but they refused to buy the same. The suit land is contiguous to the homestead land of the defendants and the consideration was fixed at 3,00,000/- (three lac) taka in presence of the mother of the plaintiff. Plaintiff received the money and gave it to his mother and put his signature on the document; that the plaintiff himself, having appeared before the Sub-registrar the document was registered as per provisions of law and the possession was delivered on the same day; that the paternal uncle of plaintiff, after having knowledge of the sale got furious and made pressure upon the mother of the plaintiff, so he had filed this suit on behalf of the plaintiff falsely alleging he is a minor.

 4. During the course of trial, the plaintiff examined 4 witnesses and the defendant examined 3 witnesses and both the parties adduced documentary as well as oral evidence to prove their respective cases.
5. The learned trial Court after perusal of the pleadings of both sides as well as upon hearing the parties and considering both oral and documentary evidences of both the parties decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 20.06.2011. 

6. Being aggrieved thereby, the defendants as appellants, preferred Title Appeal No.69 of 2011 before the Court of learned District Judge, Chandpur and subsequently the said appeal was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, 1 Court, Chandpur, for hearing and disposal and the learned Court after hearing of the appeal was pleased to allow the same by judgment and decree dated 03.02.2013, thereby reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. 

7. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree dated 03.02.2013 (decree signed on 10.2.2013) passed by, the Appellate Court in Title Appeal No.69 of 2011, allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 20.6.201 I passed by the learned trial Court, the plaintiffs has filed the instant petition under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and obtained the instant rule. 

8. Learned Advocate for the petitioner Mr. Md. Ali Reaz, appearing along with the learned Advocate Mr. Najmul Karim, having placed the petition and drawing my attention to the pleadings, the materials on record (lower Court's record), first of all submits that the impugned deed No.1219 dated 17.2.2008 (Exhibit-I of the plaintiff Exhibit-Ka of the defendants), was obtained by the defendants, while the executants Mahbub Alam (plaintiff) was a minor and also by way of coercion by detaining him in unlawful custody of the defendants and by making false assurance of giving consideration money of Tk.I,60,000.00 (one lac sixty thousand) and thus got the deed registered only on payment of Tk.14.000.00 (fourteen thousand). He mainly emphasized, in his argument, that the plaintiff was a minor at the relevant time and this has been proved by his mother Shirina Akhter; who had filed the aforesaid Title Suit No.62 of 2011, as next friend and in support of his submission, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred to a testimonial issued on 3 1.12.2002, by Alipur Government Primary School, in which his date of birth of the plaintiff was shown as 04.6.1992. He next referred to a photocopy of an application for admission, for the year 2003, signed by aforesaid Shirina Akhter, in which the date of birth of Mohammad Mahbub Alam Khan has been shown as 04.6.1992. This has been marked as Exhibit-3. The learned Advocate therefore, concludes that the date of birth of the executants Mahbub Alain Khan (plaintiff) is 04.6.1992 and he was a minor on the date of execution of the impugned deed No.1219 dated 17.2.2008. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has also referred to a Nikahnama of the mother of the plaintiff i.e. Shirina Akhter (marked as Exhibit-4), wherein the date of registration of marriage of his mother Shirina Akhter has been shown in Column No.24, as on 15.6.1990. He, therefore, submits that according to this Nikahaama and the date of registration of marriage of his mother, the executants Mahbub Alum cannot be treated as a major and as such all the documents clearly proved that at the time of registration of the impugned document, the executants Mahbub Alam was a minor. Next, referring to the Exhibit-5, which is a photocopy of the application for deleting the name of the executants Mahbub Alam from the voter list, Filed by his mother, on the ground that "কম বয়সের ছেলেকে বেশী বয়স দেখানো হয়েছে।. This application has been made by his mother Shirinal Akhter. Accordingly, he continues, considering all the documentary evidence along with the oral evidence of the plaintiff witnesses (PW I to PW4), the trial Court has rightly decreed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 20.6.2011. He also submits that there was no ground justifying the reversal of the trial Courts judgment by the Appellate Court in passing the impugned judgment and decree. He next submits that the Nikahnama, Exhibit-4, that recorded the date of registration of marriage of Shirina Akhter was not at alt discussed by the learned Appellate Court, nor any finding was given on that document and for this defect alone the impugned judgment and decree of the Appellate Court is liable to be set aside. In support of his submission, the learned Advocate fot the petitioner referred to the case of Hajee Abul Hossain and others Vs. Md. Amjad Hossain and others: 8 LG (AD) 10 and Abdullah and others Vs. Abdul Karim and others: 20 DLR (SC) 206. Accordingly, he prays for making the Rule absolute. 

9. Learned Advocate, Mr. Md. Delwar Hossein, appearing with Mr. Mohammad Bakiruddin Bhuiyan, learned Advocate and Mr. Md. Moshiur Rahman Shamim, learned Advocate, on the other hand, appearing for the opposite party (OP) Nos.l-4, having taken me through the pleadings of the parties, the oral and documentary evidence on record, first of all draws my attention to the photocopy of a testimonial, (Exhibit-2) and the photocopy of the application for admission of Mahbub Alam in Class-VI (Exhibit-3) and submits that both these documents are admittedly photocopies but no explanation has been offered as to why the plaintiff has failed to produce the original of the testimonial (Exhibit-2) or of the application for admission (Exhibit-3) before the trial Court. Referring to the Section 65 of the Evidence Act. 1872, the learned Advocate submits that there is specific provision of law as to when and how photocopies of a document i.e. secondary evidence of private document can he admitted into evidence. But, the condition laid down in Section 65 of the Evidence Act, 1872, permitting to produce secondary evidence of private documents i.e. Exhibit-2 and Exhibit-3 (photocopies) were not at all complied with. The learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos.l-4 (OP), further submits that learned lower appellate Court rightly found that the signature of mother of the plaintiff, i.e. the nest friend namely Shirina Akhter, appeared in Exhibit-3, Exhibit-5 and also on the plaint of instant Title Suit No.23 of 2008, Vokalatnama and also on the deposition sheet of PW I are not same or similar, rather these signatures. on their face, differ from each other and an examination of exhibit-5 by Court would reveal that there is no name or National ID number of the plaintiff, Mahbub Alam, in these documents. Hence, in passing the judgment and decree dated 20.6.201 I passed in Title Suit No.62 of 2011, the' learned trial Court has committed serious error of law in as much as it had failed to appreciate that these photocopies were not admissible in evidence even if no objection was raised at the time of their admission and on this ground alone the findings arrived at by the trial Court, based on photocopy documents, are liable to he reversed and set aside. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred to the case reported in 47 DLR(AD) 45: Hazi Waziullah Vs. Additional Deputy Commissioner and 54 DLR 365: Bangladesh Vs. Mirpur Semipucca Kalyan Samity. Next referring to the Exhibit-5, an application to strike out the name of the executants Mahbub Alam from the voter list, the learned Advocate submits that the provisions of Section 65 of the Evidence Act, 1872 has also been violated in respect of this document as well, whereas the trial Court has mainly relied on this document along with the Exhibit-2 and Exhibit-3, which are not at all admissible in law, as has already been settled by the apex Court. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties further submits that it is a cardinal principle of law that the plaintiff has to prove his own case and that the plaintiff cannot rely on the weakness or defect of the defence case, if any. But, in the instant case, the plaintiff has failed to prove his case and have filed all secondary evidences (photocopies) of private documents, which neither prove the execution nor the contents of those exhibited documents, as per provisions of Sections 65 and 66 of the Evidence Act, 1872. Nor the plaintiff has given any explanation, whatsoever, that the original documents were lost or destroyed. Thus the learned trial Court, he also submits that committed error of law in decreeing the suit relying upon the said non-admissible evidence. In support of his contention he has cited the cases reported in 9 BLC (AD) 220, 9 BLC(AD) 235, 47 DLR(AD) 45, 54 DLR 364, 10 BLC (AD) 58, 47 DLR 57, 14 DLR 392, 16 BLC 431, 41 DLR(AD) 97, 9 ADC(AD) 235, 42 DLR(AD) 289, 27 DLR 413, 34 DLR 278, 38 DLR 39, 44 DLR 89 and 2 BLC 376. 

10. I have heard the learned Advocates, perused the petition along with the fazul Islam & impugned judgment and considered the materials on record. 

11. I find from the record that in the very impugned kabala deed No.1219 dated 17.2.2008 (Exhibit-Kha of the defendant = Exhibit-I of the plaintiff) the plaintiff himself has admitted that his age is 20 years as on the date of execution of the deed. Moreover, this fact was corroborated by a Nikahnama (Exhibit-Kha), where the executants Mahbub Alam as the groom has admitted that his age is 24 years, vide the Nikahnama (Exhibit-Kha) registering his own marriage. In addition, having considered the impugned judgment, I find that the voter list has been taken into consideration by the Appellate Court and also discussed in its judgment holding that the voter list shows that Mahbub Alam (plaintiff/executants) was a major at the time of execution of the deed and that the voter list is a public document. Besides, it is also  on record that admitting existence of this voter list, Shirina Akhter filed an application without any date (Exhibit-5) to cancel the voter list on the ground that " কম বয়সের ছেলেকে বেশি বয়স দেথানো্ হয়েছে।” But, the name of Mahbub Alum was not mentioned in this application (Exhibit-5) filed for cancellation of the voter list. Hence, this application (photocopy) does not show that it was filed to cancel/strike out the name of Mahbub Alam. Besides, at paragraph 2 of the plaint. the plaintiff has admitted to have voluntarily executed the impugned deed stating that “বিবাদীগণের উক্ত কথায় বাদী সরল বিশ্বাসে রাজী হয়।” On the contrary, there is no statement in the plaint about Nikahnama of Shirina Akhter (Exhibit-4) or about the application for striking out the name of the plaintiff. Mahbub Alam from the voter list (Exhibit-5). As such the trial Court had no jurisdiction to allow adducing evidence on a third case, by the plaintiff or to take into consideration these two documents, in this case, by going beyond the pleadings of the plaintiff. But the trial Court has passed its judgment and decree based on a third case and on extraneous documents. Hence, the judgment and decree of the trial Court was liable to be set aside for these reasons. It is also clear that the learned trial Court. by wholly ignoring the Provisions of Section 65 of the Evidence Act, 1872, has passed the judgment and decree that was set aside in appeal. Besides, the defendants have raised objection against the Exhibit-4 by way of putting specific suggestions in cross-examination of PW-1 such as “সত্য নয় যে বিয়ের অনেক পরে কাবিন রেজিষ্টি্র হয়। সত্য নয় যে সঠিক কাবিন দাখিল করি নাই। সত্য নয় যে আমি ভূয়া কাবিন এবং কাগজপত্র দাখিল করেছি।” Similarly, regarding Exhibit-5, in the cross-examination of PW I, the defendants had put specific suggestion, such as "সত্য নহে যে ভোট দিয়েছে। ইহা সত্য নয় যে ভোটার আইডি কার্ড অনুযায়ী বর্তমানে তার বয়স ২০ বছর। ভোটার নং-৫৫৯, ওয়ার্ড নং-৯, এলাকা নং-এনায়েতপুর-১২০৯।” while the PW I in her cross-examination admitted that “আমি যে পূর্বে সাক্ষী দিয়াছি তাতে ছেলের ভোটার বাতিল করেছি কিনা তা বলি নাই। সত্য নয় যে আমি মিথ্যা ভোটার তালিকা বাতিলের কাগজ দাখিল করছি। সত্য নয় যে আমি ভূয়া কাবিন এবং কাগজ দাখিল।” As such, the Exhibit-4 and 5 could not be taken into consideration as valid evidence. In support of his contention that, the parties cannot be allowed to lead evidence in respect of matter not specifically raised in the pleadings, the learned Advocate has referred to the case of. Shamsul Haque V. Sarafat Ali: 46 DLR 57 and 27 DLR 413: Md. Ibrahim Vs. Md. Alauddin. He has also cited the decisions reported in the case of Soya Rani Guha V. Abdul Awal Miah, 41 DLR(AD) 97: and submits that even if no objection is raised, in the course of hearing, the trial Court is bound to ensure that the documentary evidence offered are admissible, i.e. as per provisions of Section 65 of the Evidence Act. These two decisions apply to the facts and circumstances of this case. I also find that Nikahnama (Exhibit-Kha) of the plaintiff, wherein he has admitted that his age is 24 years as on the date of marriage, is neither challenged nor cancelled by the plaintiff and as such the same is binding upon him and he is estoped to deny the same. Besides, the voter list, in which executants has been shown as major and which is admitted by the plaintiff by filing a so called application for cancellation of his name from the voter list, also shows that at the time of execution of Me deed the executants (plaintiff) was major. Moreover in his own admission wade in the kabala age of the executants has been recorded as 20 years. As regards the admission made in the, impugned 'kabala' and in the Nikahnama (Exhibit-Kha), both required by law to be written and registered, Section 91 of the Evidence Act, bars to adduce any oral or documentary evidence to the contrary. Moreover, voluntarily execution and registration of the impugned deed has been admitted by the plaintiff in paragraph 2 of the plaint and DW2 Rafiqul Islam, an attesting witness, has also proved that the impugned deed was executed voluntarily and for consideration. 
12. The plaintiff filed a criminal case under Sections 468/343/506 of the Penal Code and that was dismissed by the judgment dated 10.4.2014, by the Senior Judicial-Magistrate. Against the said judgment of the Criminal Court, no criminal appeal was filed. In the said judgment of the criminal Court, the executants appeared as PW2 and admitted that he has registered the impugned deed in 2008 and that he was 19 years old at that time. He has also admitted that in his Nikahnama (Exhibit-Kha) his age has been recorded as 24 years. The criminal case was filed under Sections 468/343/506 of the Penal Code and the judgment passed in that case is referable in deciding this petition as because the decision delivered in criminal case is within the exclusive jurisdiction of the criminal case, as opposed to a civil dispute decided by a criminal Court. The case of the defendants is corroborated by the evidence adduced by the plaintiff/ complainant in the said criminal case. 

13. But without appreciation of the evidence on record, the trial Court has passed the decree and the appellate Court has reversed the same after perusal of the evidence on record and upon appreciation of their legal implication. 

14. The plaintiff has failed to prove his case and obtained a decree on a case _beyond pleadings and on in admissible documents. 

15. As such, in passing the impugned judgment and decree the appellate Court has committed no error of law resulting in any error in the decision or occasioning failure of justice. I am also of the view, that the Exhibit-4 would have made no difference in the result of the appeal, even if it were specifically discussed by the appellate Court, in as much as it is negated by the Nikahnama (Exhibit-Kha). It is settled law that three conditions has to be fulfilled, as has been decided by the apex Court. in order to call the interference under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. The petitioner has failed to meet either of the three conditions laid down in Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. Mere non discussion of Exhibit-4. which is a secondary evidence nullified by Exhibit-Kha and is out of pleadings does not warrant interference in the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court. 

16. Turning my attention to the cases cited, it has been submitted by the learned Advocate for respondent that, in case of Shamsul Haque Vs. Sarafat Ali: 46 DLR 57, it has been held that cannot adduce evidence unless he pleads his case in the pleadings. In the case of Husan Ali Vs. Azmaluddin: 14 DLR 302 it has been held that the proposition that where a document was admitted in evidence by the trial Court without any objection for the other side, objection against its admissibility cannot be raised in the second appeal is not applicable when the document produced the Court is not the original document and there is no evidence that the original copy is lost nor any explanation offered for its non-production, nor the copy of the document was admitted in evidence with the consent of both the parties. The fact that it was marked in evidence without objection, would not tantamount to its being marked with the consent of the other party when it is not conceded by the lawyer of other party that the copy is a true copy of the original document. In the case of Nazi Waziullah alias Waziullah Miah Vs. The Additional Deputy Commissioner, Revenue, Noakhali: 41 DLR (AD) 97: it has been set at rest that "secondary evidence of a document is admissible in the cases specifically mentioned in Section 65 of the Evidence Act and if the original is not available, reason for non-availability must be given. Whether a party produced even through no objection was raised when it was produced." In case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Vs. Farhad Begum 9 BLC (AD) 235, it has been held -that "in order to get a decree the plaintiff must prove his own case and cannot rely on the weakness of the case of the defendants and in the present case the plaintiff failed to prove even their plaint case and introduced facts which were beyond the plaint." In case of Jashimuddin Kanchan (Md) Vs. Md. Ali Ashraf; 42 DLR (AD) 289; it has been held that "Admission of private documents as evidence — Even if no objection had been taken to formal admission of the rent receipts, the plaintiff having relied upon them for his case was bound to prove their genuineness which would be decided by the Court in the light of the facts and circumstances of the case." Then, in the case reported in 38 DLR 39; Ranjit Kumar Rakshit Vs, Shudir Kumar Chowdhury, it has been held that "the trial Court allowed the plaintiff to introduced a new story (in his deposition and by production of documents) without amending the plaint itself — Not permissible in law." 

17. In 44 DLR 89; Kazi A. Khaleque Vs. Kazi Fazlur Rahman, it has been held that "the Court will not allow either party to make any departure from the earlier pleadings set forth in the plaint or written statement." 

18. Besides, non-production of Mahbub Alam at the trial also raise a presumption against the case that he was a minor, as has been rightly pointed out by the appellate Court, although he was a competent witness's. 

19. In view of the deliberation made above and having considered the decisions cited by the parties, I am of the considered view that the plaintiff has failed to prove his case by adducing any legally admissible evidence. On the other hand, the opposite parties have been able to substantiate their case by evidence on record. 

20. Accordingly, I am of the considered view that, the appellate Court has committed no error of law in passing the impugned judgment and decree, nor it has resulted in error of law occasioning failure of justice. Hence, I find no merit in this Rule. 

21. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. 

22. The impugned judgment and decree dated 03.02.2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No.69 of 2011, reversing those dated 20.6.2011 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Matlab, Chandpur in Title Suit No.62 of 2011 is hereby upheld. 

23. No order as to costs. 

24. Send down the judgment and decree to the Court concerned with the record at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. i to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 23.7.2007 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No-36 of 2004 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing those dated 31.01.2004 passed by the learned Assistant Judge (in-charge), Jaintapur, Sylhet in Title Suit No-36 of 2000 should not be set aside. 

2. The brief fact relevant for disposal of this Rule is that the opposite party No.1, Alhaj Md. Nazim Uddin Akhter as plaintiff brought the aforesaid suit being Title Suit No. 36 of 2000 in the Court of. Assistant Judge, Jaintapur, Sylhet on 15.10.2000 for partition on the averments that the suit land was originally belonged to Safor Ali, who died leaving behind two sons namely, Sayed Ali and Bhudaya and three daughters namely, Sahar Banu, Khudban and Dudban. Thereafter, Sahar Banu died leaving her husband Mirullah and brothers and sisters. In this backdrop Mirullah, Khudban and Dudban sold .081/4 acres of land to one Hazi Abu Bakar by registered kabala dated 4.ii.i98z, who while possessing the same by constructing houses thereon transferred the same in favour of the plaintiffopposite party No. i, Alhaj Md. Nazim Uddin Akhter by registered kabala dated 01.08.1987 and handed over possession. The Plaintiff got possession less than his share and hence, the suit. 

3. Defendant Nos. 6-18 and 19-20 contested the suit by filling separate written statements upon denying the allegations of the plaintiff stated, inter-alia, that the plaintiff has/had no right, title and interest in the suit land. At the request of the plaintiff, he was allowed to construct some shops over the suit land for carrying business in the year 1982. It is further contended that the suit is not maintainable for defect of party and all the land of the tenancy has not been brought into hotchpotch. 

4. The learned Assistant Judge on the pleadings of the parties framed the following issues for determination:-

(i) Whether the suit is maintainable in its present form and manner? 

(ii) Whether the suit is bad for defect of parties or barred by principles of hotchpotch?

(iii) Whether the plaintiff has right, title and possession on the suit land? 

(iv) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get 'any relief as prayed for?  

5. At the trial the plaintiff side in all examined 6 witnesses and defendant side examined 4 witnesses and both the parties exhibited some documents to prove their respective cases. 

6. The learned Assistant Judge, Jaintapur, Sylhet by his judgment and decree dated 31.01.2004 dismissed the suit mainly on 3 (three) counts that: (i) the suit was bad for defect of parties for non-impleading all the co-sharers of the khatian in question, (ii) all the land of the tenancy has not been brought into hotchpotch (iii) plaintiff failed to prove his vendor's right, title and interest in the suit land. 

7. The unsuccessful plaintiff then preferred Title Appeal No-36 of 2004. The learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet by the impugned judgment and decree dated 23.07.2007 allowed the appeal and reversed the decision of the trial Court on the findings that after the death of Safor Ali his z sons and 3 daughters inherited .38 acres of land under Dag No.628 and Khatian No.22 in which his 3 (three) daughters were entitled to get share of .140 acres out of which they sold only .081/4 acres to the vendor of the plaintiff-petitioner. The Court of appeal below also held that the suit was neither bad for defect of parties nor barred by principles of hotchpotch as the land under Dag Nos.627 and 604 is not subject matter of the suit and the plaintiff by adducing evidence has been succeeded to prove his right, title and possession in the suit land. 

8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment 'and decree dated 23.7.2007 passed by the learned Additional District Judge 3rd Court Sylhet in Title Appeal yo.3g,of,Aga the present defendant petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

9. Mr. J. N. Deb, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant petitioner submits that the court of appeal below while decreeing the suit failed to consider that the suit was bad for defect of parties inasmuch as from Exhibit-2, Patta no. 74 there are as many as 26 Pattaders, all of them were not impleaded in the present suit for partition and as such committed an error of law which resulted in an error in the decision and occasioned failure of justice. He next submits that the Court of appeal below while decreeing the suit failed to appreciate that it appears from Patta No. 74, containing dag nos. 407 and 898 which subsequently recorded in Khatian No. 22 with dag Nos. 627, 604 and 628 having an area of .26, .17 and .38 acres respectively and all these lands except Dag No. 628 were not brought into the present suit and thereupon, the suit is bad for non-inclusion of all the ejmali property in the suit and as such committed an error of law which resulted in an error in the decision and occasioned failure of justice. 

10. Mr. J. N. Deb, in the course of his argument upon placing the deposition of witnesses and exhibits submits that the court of appeal below while decreeing the suit failed to consider that neither there was any partition between the heirs of Safor Ali nor Safor Ali was the exclusive owner of the disputed Patta and Khatian and as such the transfer dated 04.11.1982 by some of the heirs of Safor Ali in favour of Abu Bakkar was illegal and mere paper transaction. He further submits that the Court of appeal below while decreeing the suit failed to appreciate that the defendant side by adducing evidence has been able to prove that the plaintiff is nothing but a permissive possessor and as such committed an error of law which resulted in an error in the decision and occasioned failure of justice. Mr. Deb, finally argues that the plaintiffs suit for partition is not maintainable inasmuch as admittedly daughters of deceased Safor Ali transmitted the suit property from an undivided plot without any amicable partition and admittedly no records of right was prepared in the name of the daughters of deceased Safor Ali rather, the records of right prepared in the name of the sons of deceased Safor Ali and as such the instant suit for simple partition without a prayer for declaration of title in the suit property is not maintainable. Mr. J. N. Deb in support of his submission relies on the decisions reported in 43 DLR(AD) 87, 49 DLR(AD) 68, 51 DLR(AD) 155, 10 PLR(Dhaka)27 and 6 BLD(AD) 109. 

11. Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1, on the other hand, by filing counter affidavit contested the Rule. The learned Advocate at the very outset drawing my attention to the impugned judgment submits that admittedly the suit land was originally belonged by Safor Ali, who died leaving behind three daughters and two sons and for urgent need of money the 3 (three) daughters of Safor Ali transferred the suit land to the vendor of present petitioner and the Court of appeal below on due consideration of the materials and evidence on record arrived at a findings that: 

“২২নং খতিয়ানের ৬২৮ দাগের ৩৮ শতক ভূমির বিপরীতে দুবাই এর নাম লিপি থাকার কারনে অপর পুত্র সাইদ আলী ও তিন কন্যা শহরবান, কুদবান, ও দুধবান ওয়ারিশী বা ফরায়াজী স্তত্বাংশ লোপ পাওয়ার কোন কারন নাই। তাহারা পিতা-মাতার ত্যজ্যবিত্তে তাহাদের ওয়ারিশী হিস্যা সর্বাবস্থায় পাইতে হকদার ও অধিকারী হয় বটে। ৬২৮ দাগের ভূমির পরিমান ৩৮ শতক। সফর আলীর দুই পুত্র ও ৩ কন্যার মধ্যে উক্ত ৩৮ শতক ভূমি ফরায়েজ মোতাবেক বিলি বন্টন হইলে প্রত্যেক পুত্রের হিস্যা হয় ১০ ৬/৭ শতক এবং প্রত্যেক কন্যার হিস্যা হয় ৫ ৩/৭ শতক। সফর আলী কন্যা শহরবানু বিবি ৫ ৩/৭ শতক ভূমিতেমা���িক থাকিয়া স্বামী মনীর উল্যা, দুই ভ্রাতা ও দুই বোনকে ওয়ারিশ রাখিয়া মারা যান। শহরবানের কোন পুত্র কন্যা না থাকায় স্বামী মীর উল্যা ২/১ অংশ হিসাবে ২ ৫/৭ শতক ভূমি পাইবে। অনুরুপ ভাবে শহরবান বিবির দুই বোন কুদবান ও দুধবান বিবি একত্রে ১৯/২১ শতক ভূমি পাইবে। এই হিসেবে নকুদবান, দুধবান ও মীর উল্ল্যার মোট সম্পত্তি হয় ৫ ৩/৭+৫ ৩/৭ +  ১৯/২১+ ২ ৩/৭= ১৪ ১০/২১ শতক। এই কুদবান বিবি, দুধবান বিবি ও মীর উল্লাহ একত্রে নালিশী ৬২৮ দাগের ৩৮ শতকের অন্দরে পশ্চিমাংশে ৮ ১/৪ শতক ভূমি গত ৪/১১/৮২ তারিখে সম্পাদিত ও রেজিষ্ট্রিকৃত ১৯৯৯ নং সাফ কবলা মূলে হাজী আবু বকরের নিকট বিক্রয় করেন। ১৯৯৯/৮২ নং রেজিষ্ট্রি সাফ কবালা প্রদর্শনী-৬ হিসাবে আপীলকারী বাদী পক্ষে দাখিল আছে। সফর আলীর ওয়ারিশ হিসাবে এই কবালার দাতা কুদবান বিবি, দুধবান বিবি ও মীর উল্লা ৬২৮ দাগের ৩৮ শতক ভুমির অন্দরে কমবেশী ১৪ ১০/২১ শতক ভুমিতে মালিক স্বত্ববান থাকিয়া তদমধ্যে পশ্চিমাংশে ৮ ১/৪ শতক ভূমি বাদীর বায়া হাজী আবু বকরের নিকট বিক্রয় করেন। এই ১৯৯৯/৮২ নং রেজিষ্ট্রি সাফ কবালাটি একটি বৈধ পনপ্রবৃত্তি যুক্ত ও কার্যকরী দলিল হয়। and upon such findings the learned District judge clearly found the right, title and possession of the plaintiffs vendor Haji Abu Bakkar and consequently, rightly decreed the suit after setting-aside the judgment of the trial Court. He next submits that all the Ms. namely PW-1, PW2, PW-3, PW-4, PW-5 and PW-6 in their respective testimony categorically stated that the present plaintiff-opposite party purchased the suit land on 01.4.1987 from Haji Abu Bakkar1by'a-feglgttited deed and since then he has been possessing the suit land by paying rent, taxes to the Government regularly. He further submits that the Court of appeal below on proper assessment of the evidence and materials on record rightly held that trial judge was absolutely wrong in holding that the suit is not maintainable without a prayer for partition of the whole tenancy, and without impleading all the parties interested in the land of the jama inasmuch as the opposite party No. i (plaintiff) is only the purchaser of the suit land and the suit land is related only Dag No. 628 and the heirs of Safer Ali and all the claimants related to the Dag No. 628 have been made party in the instant Civil Revision and on that account the suit is neither bad for defect of parties nor bad for non-inclusion of all the ejmali property. With this regard he adds that law is well settled in this regard that when parties to the partition suit have no common interest in a particular property, the same need not be included in the schedule of the plaint and when all the parties of particular Khatian have no common interest in respect of partition, their names do not require to bring in the schedule of the plaint and the Court of appeal below after a detailed discussion of all these aspects of the case rightly decreed the suit and as such the same should not be disturbed. Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman in support his argument relies on the decision reported in 52 DLR(AD) 34, 33 DLR(AD) 347, 55 DLR(AD) 115, 49 DLR(AD) 151, 28 DLR(AD) 61, 2 BLC(AD) 135 and 5 BLC(AD) 76. 

12. I have heard the learned Advocates for the respective parties and perused the judgments of 2 Courts below and other materials on record including deposition of witnesses and exhibits. Now, to deal with the contentions raised by the parties before this Court it would be convenient for me to decide first of all the question of maintainability of the partition suit filed by the opposite party no.1. 

13. On perusal of the materials on record, it appears that admittedly the suit property originally belonged by one Safor Ali, who died leaving behind two sons and three daughters and later on, two daughters of Safor Ali and one Mirullah, husband of Sahar Banu transferred .081/4 acres of land to Haji Abu Bakkar by registered deed dated 4.11.1982 without any partition or amicable settlement between the heirs of deceased Safor Ali and thereafter, the said Haji Abu Bakkar ( PW-i) transferred the suit land to plaintiff -appellant-opposite party by executing a registered deed dated 01.4.1987. It further appears from Exhibit-2& Exhibit-Ka, Patta No-74, the name of Safor Ali struck off by replacing Pattader No-14, Sayed Ali and Pattader No-15, Budai as per order dated 16.07.1938 and corrected the same vide order dated 14.10.1938, which proved that Safor Ali was no longer remains pattader and the name of Syed Ali also subsequently has been struck off by replacing Pattader Nos. 17-21, vide order dated 12.06.1941 and corrected the same by order dated 16.12.1941. It also appears from Exhibit-7, D.P. Khatian No.zz and Exhibit - (Kha) Printed S.A. Khatian No. 27 that the same prepared in the name of Boudai Miah, son of Safor All along with others but neither in the Patta No. 74 nor in S.A. Khatian the name of the daughters of Safor All were recorded and the contents of the deed dated 4.11.1982 do not, disclose that the daughters of Safor Ali transferred their share out of .38 acres of land under Dag No.628 and Khatian No.22 inherited by z(two) sons and 3(three) daughters of Safor  Ali. Therefore, I am unable to agree with the finding of the Court of appeal below that the trial Court committed illegality in holding that the plaintiff failed to prove his vendor's or predecessor's exclusive possession and title in the suit land. 

14. Upon an exhaustive consideration of the oral and documentary evidence on record, I find nothing on record to suggest that the daughters of Safor Ali had any exclusive right, title and possession in the suit land and the records of right also not prepared in their name though the Court of appeal below at its own motion arrived at a finding that after the death of Safor Ali his 2 sons and 3 daughters inherited .38 acres of land of Dag No.628 corresponding to Khatian No.22 and as such 3 (three) daughters were entitled to get share of 1410/21 acres out of which they sold only .081/4 acres to the vendor of the plaintiff-petitioner. I have already indicated that there being nothing on record to suggest that the daughters of Safor Ali were in exclusive possession at any time over the suit land and admittedly, the daughters of Safor Ali without any partition transferred their unspecified share on the basis of their own calculation though from Exhibit-2, Patta No.74 it appears that the name of Safor Ali has been struck off by replacing his sons being Pattader No-14 Sayed Ali and Pattader No.I5, Budai as per order of the revenue authority dated 16.07.1938 and neither in the Patta No. 74 nor in S.A. Khatian the name of the alleged daughters of Safor Ali were mentioned in any manner. Practically, from the evidence on record so far right, title and possession of the alleged the daughters of Safor Ali in the suit land is nil. SO, the reasons given by the learned judge of the lower appellate Court for passing the decree in favour of the plaintiff is not sustainable either in law or on facts. 

15. The trial Court after a detailed discussion of the evidence of the plaintiff and defendants and attending circumstances borne out by records held that the plaintiff failed to prove their predecessor's/ vendor's exclusive title and possession in the suit land. The Court of appeal below reversed the findings of the trial Court by the impugned judgment stating that if Boudi and Syed Ali as heirs of Safar All got the land of Safar Ali, the daughters of Safar Ali obviously be entitled to get their shaham as a legal heirs of Safar All according to the personal law and hence, the transfer in question by registered deed dated 4.11.1982 in favour of Haji Abu Bakker was a valid transfer and, on this finding the learned Additional District Judge, 3N Court, Sylhet decreed the suit. In the facts and circumstance of the case this finding of the lower appellate Court is not based on correct evaluation of the facts and materials of the case not on proper appreciation of the evidence on record. It is very surprising that the learned judge of the lower appellate Court enunciated a wrong proposition of law by giving a go-by to the material evidence on record. This is not only illegal but also not a proper exercise of jurisdiction vested in the Court. 

16. In a suit for partition the Court will no doubt consider the title of the plaintiff to the suit land in some details. In this case I have already noticed that the title of the plaintiffs predecessors/vendors to the partible property is not clear, the suit for simple partition is not maintainable without declaration of title. 

17. Having realized the difficulty, the learned Advocate Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman, relying on the decisions reported in 55 DLR(AD) 115 and 33 DLR(AD) 347 submits that in view of the long possession of the plaintiff in the suit land there is no necessity for getting or asking declaration of title and as such the present suit is well maintainable without any prayer for declaration of title. With this regard he adds that in a suit for partition all the incidental question of title, however complicated it may be decided and finally disposed of. 

To meet this branch of argument of Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman, I have carefully studied those decisions to the best of my ability and find that the principles laid down in those decisions are not applicable in the present case inasmuch as facts of those cases are quite distinguishable from the facts of the case in hand. Therefore, I find no substance in either of the contentions as raised by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party No.1. In view of my finding on the question of maintainability of the case itself it is needless to go into the other points. 

18. For the reasons stated above the judgment of the lower appellate Court does not deserve to be sustained. 

19. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and decree dated 23-7.2007 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court,  Sylhet in Title Appeal No-36 Of 2004 is set-aside. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. However, the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 shall still approach the Court if he so likes to consider his case. 

20. Let a copy of the judgment along with the lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.
