full_judgment:
Mr. Borhanuddin, J :- This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree complained of in the application should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party No.1 instituted Title Suit No.249 of 1984 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kurigram for declaration of title on correction of record of right. Plaintiff's case in short is that the suit land originally belonged to Ibrahim Sheikh and Ishaque Sheikh in equal 8 annas share. Ibrahim Sheikh died leaving two sons Azizur Rahman and Insar Ali who inherited him. Ishaque Sheikh died leaving only son Nizamuddin who inherited 8 annas share of his father in the suit property. Nizamuddin died leaving wife Habija Bewa and daughter Hasina Banu. During possession they sold 4.49 decimals of land to Alauddin vide registered kabala dated 08.01.1948. In his turn Alauddin transferred 3.17 decimals of land to the plaintiff vide registered patta taking salami of taka 970/-. Since then the plaintiff is in possession of tfiElliand7Due to illness the plaintiff could not appear before the settlement employees during last survey and as such S.A. Khatian No.64 wrongly 4 recorded in the name of defendants. Plaintiff came to know about the wrong recording when he went to pay rent to the Tahasil office. Hence, the present suit.

3. Defendant Nos.1-3 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint and contending inter alia that their father purchased 4.49 decimals of land from Habiza Bewa and others vide registered kabala dated 08.01.1948 and subsequently settled the land to the plaintiff. Plaintiff surrendered the land in 13.60 B.S. by giving ishtafanama being unable to pay rent. Since then the defendants are in possession of the suit land and S.A. Khatian prepared accordingly. Plaintiff has no title and possession over the suit land. With such averments they prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

4. During pendency of the Rule the opposite party Nos.3-6 added themselves in the instant civil revision by filing an application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The case of the added opposite parties are that the suit jote appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.76 measuring an area of 8.45 acres was originally belonged to Ibrahim Sheikh and Ehsan in equal 8 annas share. While possessing his 8 annas share ( Ibrahim died leaving wife Gendi Bewa, two sons Azizar Rahman and Ensar Ali and one daughter Buri Khatun. Thereafter Ehsan died leaving only son Abul Kashem. Abul Kashed died leaving two sons Solaiman All and Bablu Miah and one daughter Aklima Khatun. Azizar Rahman, one of the son of late Ibrahim Sheikh, died unmarried. Then Gendi Bewa died leaving one son Ensar Ali and one daughter Buri Khatun. Ensar Ali and Burl Khatun have been possessing 8 annas share of the suit jote left by their father Ibrahim Sheikh. 8 annas share of Ehsan now under the possession of his two sons and one daughter Solaiman, Bablu and Aklima Khatun. Nizamuddin son of Arabuddin Mohammad had no interest in the suit jote and had no title and possession over the suit jote. From C.S. Khatian No.10 of Mouza Dakkhin Basjani, it is apparent that Nizamuddin Munshi, Ehsanuddin Sheikh, Ibrahim Sheikh, Zahiruddin Sarkar and Jonab Uddin Sarkar are the sons of Arabuddin Mohammad and Nizamuddin 'was not the son of Ehsanuddin. Kabala of the plaintiff is fraudulent and collusive. The heirs of C.S. tenant Ibrahim Sheikh" and Ehsan are now possessing the suit land and the opposite party. Nos.3-6 have been possessing their respective share along with the heirs of Ehsan but' those persons were not made parties. 

5. At the time of hearing of the Rule, learned Advocate for the petitioners filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure for producing two rent receipts of Khatian No.64 of the suit land as additional evidence before this court. It is stated in the application that father of this applicant late Rafigul Hoque defendant witness No.1 made his deposition before the trial court and at the time he handed over the rent receipts of Khatian No.64 to his learned Advocate for submitting in the court but the learned Advocate inadvertently did not submit the documents in the court for which the rent receipts has not been marked as Exhibits in the case record. It is stated in the application that the learned Advocate inadvertently did-not submit the rent receipts in the trial court but it appears that the defendant-petitioners did not take any step to file the rent receipts in the appellate court below though they had ample opportunity to produce the same before the appellate court below. The provisions of order 41 rule 27 are clearly not intended to allow a litigant who has been unsuccessful in the lower court to patch up the weak parts of his case and fill up the omissions in the revisional court and as such the application for additional evidence is not necessary at this point of time to pronounce judgment. 

6. Mr. Md. Mosiul Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submit that the courts below failed to consider that the patta executed on 24 Falgun 1354 B.S. by Alauddin in favour of the plaintiff was for a limited period and the Patta was not executed by both lessee and lessor and as such it is 'not a valid patta. He submits that the plaintiff produced certified copy of the patta without any explanation as to the original of the same and as such accepting the secondary evidence is not proper and legal. He also submits that the plaintiff filed suit for declaration without seeking any consequential relief and as such the suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. He submits that a patta unless executed by both the lessor and lessee is void under Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act and without considering this legal aspect the appellate court below committed an error of law which occasioned failure of justice. He also submits that the impugned judgment and decree is bad for non-consideration of the material evidence and misreading of evidence on record and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He submits that the revisional court is competent to interfere in a case of non-consideration of material evidence which is specifically material for determination of the material issue. He further submits that the plaintiff neither avail to record their names in the Record of Rights nor they have proved their tenancy as a holding over and without considering this legal aspect the appellate court below committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice. In support of his submissions, the learned Advocate referred to the case of Abdus Sattar and others vs. Suresh Chandra Das and others, reported in 32 DLR (AD) 170; the case of Syed Imteyazuddin Hossain vs. Md. Abdul Majid, reported in 22 DLR 451; Sheikh Md. Siddique vs. Hari Lal Nath and others, reported in 22 DLR 359; the case of Narendra Nath Pal vs. Abdur Rahman Molla, reported in 26 DLR 45; the case of Noor Mohammad Khan and others vs. Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others, reported in 42 DLR 434; the case of Dudu Mia and other vs. Ekram Miah Chowdhury and others, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 7; the case of Bina Rani and another vs. Shantosh Chandra Dey, reported in 51 DLR(AD) 81 and the case of Safaruddin and others vs. Fazlul Huq and others, reported in 49 DLR (AD) 151. 

7. On the other hand Subash Chandra Saha, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos.1(a) to 1(m) submits that both the courts below concurrently arrived at a finding that the defendants failed to prove ishtafanama relating to surrender of land by the plaintiff and as such both the courts below decreed the suit. He also submits that when the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land seeking declaration of title to the suit land, he need not seek any further relief as has been contemplated by the proviso to Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. He also submits that the findings of fact cannot be interfered with in revisional jurisdiction unless the same is absolutely perverse. He further submits that there is no infirmity or ambiguity in the judgment passed by the appellate court below and as such there is nothing to interfere with. In support of his submissions, the learned Advocate referred to the case of Nurul Haque and another NS. Lutfor Rahman and others, reported in 10 BLT(AD) 173  the case of Md. Mansur Ali vs. Helaluddin Bhuiyan and another, reported in 2 MLR(AD) 363; the case of Md. Shahjahan Mizi and others vs. Md. Shamsul Hoque Mizi and others, reported in 4 MLR(HC) 273 and the case of Khurshid Ali and others vs. Noorjahan Bewa and others, reported in 1 MLR(AD) 210. 

8. Mr. Humayun Hossain Khadem, learned Advocate appearing for the .added opposite party Nos.3-6 submits that the kabala of the plaintiff is fraudulent and collusive. He also submits that Nizamuddin was the son of Arabuddin Mohammad and he had no interest in the suit jote and he had no title and possession over the suit land and as such the plaintiff cannot purchase the suit land from Nizamuddin or his heirs since Nizamuddin had no title and possession over the suit land. He further submits that the plaintiff's claim that they had purchased the property from the heirs of said Nizamuddin but in fact their claim is unfounded and false. 

9. Heard the learned Advocates. Perused the revisional application, application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, supplementary affidavit, judgment of the courts below and the materials available in the lower court record. 

10. From the application filed under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure and also from the Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the added opposite party Nos.3- 6 it appears that the added opposite' parties brought completely a new fact other than the facts on which both the courts below disposed of the suit. Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is concerned with an error of law committed by the trial court and appellate court below. The revisional court cannot decide a contested question of fact raised for the first time in revision. Since it is stated in the supplementary affidavit that the added opposite parties have been possessing their respective shares, they can file a suit for partition or declaration of title or otherwise if they are so advised. 

11. It appears that both the parties admits that Alauddin, predecessor of the defendants, settled the suit land to the plaintiff vide registered patta. Discord between the parties started thereafter. Plaintiff claims that he took settlement of the land vide registered patta and since then he is in possession of the suit land. He further claims that due to illness the plaintiff could not appear before the settlement employees during last survey and as such S.A. Khatian No.64 wrongly recorded in the name of defendants and he came to know about the wrong recording when he went to pay rent to the Tahasil Office. On the other hand the definite case of the defendant Nos.1-3 is that plaintiff surrendered the suit land in 1360 B.S. by giving ishtafanama being unable to pay rent and since then the defendants are in possession of the suit land. S.A. Khatian prepared accordingly. I have carefully and meticulously gone through the judgment passed by the courts below. It appears that the learned Assistant Judge after framing proper issues and after threadbare discussions on the issues arrived at a finding : 
“বিবাদীপক্ষের ১নং স্বাক্ষী তাহার জবানবন্দিতে বলেন বাদী তাহার পাওনা জমি বাবদ খাজনা চালাইতে অসমর্থ হইলে উত্তর দা���দ বিবাদীপক্ষের নিকট লিখিত ইস্তফা প্রদান করেন। কিন্তু বিবাদীপক্ষ বাদী কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত কোন লিখিত ইস্তফা দাখিল করেন নাই। লিখিত ইস্তফা দাখিল ছাড়া বাদী উক্ত জমি বিবাদী পক্ষ বরাবর ইস্তফা দিয়াছিলেন কিনা তাহা আমার বোধগম্য নহে। ইহাও প্রমানিত হয় যে, বাদী আদৌ বিবাদীপক্ষ বরাবর কোন ইস্তেফাপত্র প্রদান করেন নাই বা উক্ত বিষয় বিশ্বাসযোগ্য নহে। কাজেই নালিশী জমিতে বিবাদীপক্ষের স্বত্ত্ব আছে তাহা প্রমানিত হয় না।”

The learned Subordinate Judge after reassessing the evidence on record independently arrived at a finding :
“বিবাদীপক্ষের সুনির্দিষ্ট দাবি হইল যে, বাদীপক্ষ নালিশী জমি পত্তন গ্রহন করার পর খাজনা চালাইতে অসমর্থ হইলে উত্তরদায়ক বিবাদীপক্ষের নিকট লিখিতভাবে ইস্তফা প্রদান করেন। বিবাদীর উক্ত বক্তব্য বাদীর পত্তন গ্রহন ও দখলের বিষয়টি স্বীকৃত হইয়াছে। লিখিত ইস্তফা প্রদানের বিষয়টি বিবাদীপক্ষের উপর প্রমানের দায়িত্ব কিন্তু বিবাদীপক্ষ উক্ত লিখিত ইস্তফা প্রমানে সমর্থ হন নাই। সুতরাং নালিশী ভূমি হাল রেকর্ডে বিবাদীর নামে লিপিবদ্ধ হইলেও উক্ত লিখিত ইস্তফা প্রদানের প্রামান্য কাগজের অভাবে বাদীর স্বত্ত্বকে প্রমান করে।”
It is well settled principle in law that the High Court Division in exercise of revisional jurisdiction under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure shall not ordinarily interfere with the concurrent findings of fact recorded by the courts below unless it appears to it that the courts below patently committed an illegality and took a wrong view of law, as a result of which they arrived at erroneous finding of fact by illegal exercise of jurisdiction. In many cases our apex court held :

"It is not justified to interfere with the concurrent findings recorded by the courts below." 

12. The plaintiff has filed the suit for declaration of title on assertion that he is in possession of the suit land and the recording of S.A. Khatian No.64 is wrong. Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act provides that a suit for mere declaration of any legal character or any right to property is maintainable. In view of the evidence of possession in favour of the plaintiff, the plaintiff need not ask for any further relief. In view of the matter, I am of the opinion that present suit for mere declaration is maintainable. 

13. The submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the patta was not executed by both parties and it is for a limited period are beyond the pleadings of the case and as such the same is not require to be addressed in this revisional jurisdiction. 

14. Going through the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Kurigram, I do not find any findings of fact recorded by the court below are perverse and there has been non-application of mind. 

15. Under the facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated above, I do find any reason to interfere with the judgment and decree dated 30.05.1991 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Kurigram, in Other Appeal No.73 of 1988 affirming the judgment and decree dated 03.05.1988 passed by the learned Assistant Judge in Other Suit No.249 of 1984. 

16. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. 

17. Send down the lower court record. 

End.

Mr. A. M. Mahmudur Rahman, J:-This application for review of the judgment delivered by me on June 15, 1993 in Civil Revision No. 2847 of 1992. 

2. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that while delivering the judgment I did not consider exhibit 7, the report to the Advocate Commissioner, which was accepted by the trial court independently on contest and there occurs an error of law apparent on the face of the record which calls for review of the judgment. He also submits that order of remand of this court to consider Ext. 7 by the court below will only protract the litigation between the parties and this court is to exercise its inherent power in considering Ext, 7 and review the judgment. 

3. Neither non-consideration of material evidence nor prolongation of litigation is a ground for review within the meaning of S. 114 and Or. 47 C.P.C. As the courts below failed to consider Ext. 7, this court in order to arrive at a finding on fact upon consideration of such evidence by the court below remanded the case. At best non-consideration of Ext. 7, a material evidence, by this court may be considered to be a ground for appeal but not a ground for review. There is no substance in this application. 

4. Accordingly, this application is rejected in liming. No costs. 1994 (II) BLT (HCD) 39 High Court 

	End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Mamtaz Uddin Ahmed, J : This is an application under article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh challenging the Order Nos.12- 
14 dated 09.09.2007, 07.10.2007 and 22.10.2007 passed by the learned Judge Artha Rin Adalat No.4 at Dhaka in Artha Zari Suit No.336 of 2006 (Annexure-A). 

2. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the writ petitioner has taken us through the writ petition and the annexure and submits that the Artha Rin Adalat has passed the impugned Order Nos.12-14 in gross violation of the provision of sub-section (1)(2)(3)(4) and 5(3) of section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and as such, the impugned orders are liable to declared to have passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The learned Advocate further submitted that the learned Judge has not complied with the provision of section 33 to its entirety but passed the impugned order and as such, the impugned order is liable to be declared to have 'passed without lawful authority and is no legal effect. 

3. Referring to the case reported in 15 BLT (HCD) 425 the learned Advocate submits that "Sub-section 7 envisages vesting of ownership of the property of the Judgment debtor upon the decree holder. The said vesting of ownership includes delivery of possession of the property. Without delivery of possession, the execution case cannot be disposed of and as such the impugned order is liable to be declared to have passed without lawful authority and is no legal effect. 

4. Mr. Mustafa Jaman Islam, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the respondents submits that the learned Judge of the Adalat has rightly passed the impugned order which calls for no interference by this Hon'ble Court.

5. Heard the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the parties and perused the writ petition. 

6. On perusal of the impugned order, it appears that the learned Judge has passed the order No.14. “ডিক্রিদার পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবী অর্থৃঋণ আদালত আইন ২০০৩ এর ৩৩(৫) ধারা মদে সার্টিফিকেট গ্রহণ করেছেন।
অতএব,
আদেশ হয় যে অত্র মোকদ্দমা পূর্ণ সন্তষ্টিতে নিস্পত্তি করা হলো।
আমার কথিত মতে 
স্বা/-অস্পষ্ট 						স্বা/-অস্পষ্ট 
জজ অর্থঋণ আদালত নং-৪ ঢাকা।			জজ অর্থঋণ আদালত নং-৪ ঢাকা।

but has not passed the order as contemplated under section 33(7). Consequently, the title and possession of the mortgaged property has not been vested in the decree holder and without vesting a property, the execution case cannot be disposed of. 

7. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner but we are not inclined to issue rule for procedural mistake. In order to render substantial justice, it would be proper to set aside the impugned order and accordingly, the impugned order is set aside and the Artha Rin Adalat is directed to proceed in accordance with law. 

8. With the aforesaid findings and observations, the writ petition is summarily disposed of, without any order as to casts.

End.

caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 697 of 1991 with connected Civil Rule No.416 (FM)/1991
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Mozaffar Hossain with Mr. Md. Abdur Rahim. Advocate ------ For the appellant.
Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim with Mr. Zahedul Bari. Advocates ------ For respondent No. 1.
parties:
Imtiaj Ali ------ Appellant.
Vs.
Eskander Mirja ------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
Mr. Mahmudul Amin Chowdhury, J:-This appeal is by the defendant-appellant against the order of rejection of Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 1987 filed under Order 9. Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

2. The short fact leading to this miscellaneous case is that the respondent instituted other Class Suit No. 46 of 1986 in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra against the present appellant and another for specific performance of Contract. That suit was ultimately decreed ex parte. Thereafter the present appellant filed Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 1987 under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and prayed for setting aside the ex parte decree on the ground that summons of the suit were not served upon any of the defendants rather the same was suppressed. 

3. In the miscellaneous case the plain-tiff-respondent entered appearance and filed a written objection denying the allegations contending inter alia that sum- 1 months of the original Other Class Suit No. 46 of 1986 were duly served upon the defendants including the present appellant who was hold for statutory attorney. It is their further case that summons of the suit were also served by registered post and since there was nothing to cons test the suit. The defendants in spite of service of summons failed to appear on the date fixed. Consequently the suit was.' decreed ex parte and the decree was ultimately executed in O.0 Execution Case No. 6 of 1986 and another O.C. Execution Case No. 11 of 1986 is pending which was filed for recovery of the costs. 

4. Before the trial Court both the parties adduced oral and documentary evidence in support of their respective cases. The learned Subordinate Judge then by his judgment dated 26.8.91 dismissed the miscellaneous case and refused to set aside the ex parte decree. The defendant No 1 of the original suit then preferred this appeal before this Court. 

5. Mr. Mozaffar Hossain along with Mr. M.A. Rahim, the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the appellant and they submitted that the summons upon the defendants have not been served rather those are suppressed even there was no service of summons by registered post as required under the law and by suppressing the summons the plaintiff secured the ex parte decree. It has been contended that the decree was obtained in haste will be evident from the fact that the suit was filed on 29.1.86 and the ex parte decree was obtained on 13.3.86 and this haste indicate that fraud was practiced upon the Court by the plaintiff in securing the decree. The learned Advocate contends that by misleading the Court the present ex parte decree has been obtained. The learned Advocate further submits that if the evidence adduced from the side of the opposite party-respondents adduced in the miscellaneous case is considered it will appear that there was no service of summons. 

6. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plain-tiff-respondents on the other hand submits that the evidence of O.P. Ws. 2 and 3 coupled with the service return proved that when the defendants refused to accept the summons those are served by hanging which were accepted by the trial Court as sufficient service and as such there was no suppression of summons. He further submitted that when the constituted attorney refused to accept the summons it may be construed as proper ser-vice and that has been done in the original suit, that the learned Advocate further contends that the miscellaneous case was filed not by the petitioner herself but through her constituted attorney and then as the power of attorney that was submit-ted before the court was not revalided in this country that cannot be considered and as such it may be construed that the miscellaneous case was not filed by the present appellant herself and some other interested persons are working behind the scene. 

7. The respondent instituted O.C. Suit No. 46 of 1986 before the learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra for Specific Performance of Contract and his case is that he entered into a contract with the present appellant for purchase of the suit property at a consideration of Tk. 16,25,000.00 and he was inducted into possession when the entire consideration money was paid and there was a stipulation that on obtaining income tax clearance certificate the kabala would be executed. But as the appellant failed to exe-cute and register the kabala the plaintiff had instituted the suit for Specific Performance of Contract. 

8. The present miscellaneous case has been filed on the ground of obtaining the ex parte decree in the original suit on suppression of the summons. The respondent raised an objection that the power of attorney which was produced before the trial Court and the attorney who was instrumental in filling the miscellaneous case has not been revalidated in this country and no one can act on the basis of that power of attorney and from that the learned Advocate for the respondent tried to impress that the miscellaneous case cannot be maintained. It appears from the impugned judgment that the power of attorney Ext. 6 is a product of fraud and forgery and the petitioner never executed it, and therefore, P.W. 1 is neither attorney nor a Karjakarak of the appellant. The trial Court it appears took great pain in discarding the power of attorney and after discarding the same came to the finding that the present case has not been filed by the appellant. But it is well settled that when the Court finds that the power of attorney is bad, the only order that the Court can pass is under Order HI, Rule 4(1). The Court shall debar the Advocate to act for the party in the Court, for the simple reason that he has not been appointed for the purpose by or under a valid power of attorney and has therefore, no authority to act on behalf of the party in the Court. The disability attaches to the Advocate and not to the plaint. In such circumstances the court will next sit a date for steps to be taken by the plaintiff and on the next date several options are open to the plaintiff. He may appear in person or by another recognised agent or by the same recognised agent after removing the objections that have been taken with regard to the validity of the power of attorney. It has been held in the case of Anath Bandhu Guha & Sons Ltd., through its attorney Md. Sirajul Huq Vs. Babu Sudhangshu Shekhar Haider, reported in 42 D.L.R. (AD) 244, that when the power of attorney fails the embargo that follows will fall upon the Advocate and not on prosecution of the suit by the principal. This disability attaches to the Advocate not to the plaint. 

9. It appears from the record that the trial Court on the face of objection from the present respondents directed for the personal appearance of the petitioner, but thereafter the petitioner produced a power of attorney which was not accepted as valid and correct power of attorney by the trial Court. But in such circumstances the trial Court ought to have direct for further correct and better power of attorney but instead of doing that the Court proceeded with the disposal of the miscellaneous case. The Court found that the power of attorney is forged and fabricated. May be it was forged and fabricated but that can-not be a ground for dismissal of the miscellaneous case in view of the aforesaid decision of our Appellate Division. 

10. Now the main contention of the appellant is that the summons of the original suit were suppressed. The learned Advocate for the appellant led us through the service return and submitted that the return clearly indicate that summons were suppressed. To prove the service of summons the respondent examined two witnesses and they are O.P. Ws. 2 and 3. O.P.W. 2 is an attesting witness and O.P.W. 3 is the process server. 

11. We have carefully gone through the service return which has been marked as Ext Ka, where the process server reported that he went to the defendant's residence and when the husband of defendant No. 1 refused to accept the summons it was served by hanging. From this process server it appears that the process server was directed to service of summons on two defendants, one is the present appellant and the other one is defendant No. 2 her husband. But the service of return does not indicate that the process server was attended to service of summons on defendant No. 2. This process server deposed as O.P.W. 3. In his examination-in-chief he stated that he has served the summons on the defendant, but he has not stated on oath that he tried to serve the summons of both the defendants and when they refused to accept the same was served by hanging. The process server is silent on mode of service of summons or attempt to service of summons on defendant No. 2. If the evidence is considered it would appear that the summons were served only on the one defendant, Though a matter of fact there was two defendants. O.P.W. 2 appeared before the trial Court as an attesting witness on ser-vice of summons. He in his examination-in-chief stated that the process server in his presence served the summons on Abdur Rashid Khan who is admittedly defendant No. 2. He has not stated a single word on the service of summons on defendant No. 1. So, it appears that three versions came up before the trial Court on service of summons, one is the Ext. Ka the service return, the second one is the evidence of O.P.W. 3 and 3rd one is the evidence of O.P.W. 2 the attesting witness. It appears from the record that after the receipt of this return the trial Court fixed a date for ex parte disposal. But before fixing a date the trial Court has not looked into the service return. This is one part of the state of affairs as regards service of summons on the defendants. 

12. The second part is that after the insertion of the rule 19A and 19B of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure, it appears that when a suit is filed the Court shall, in addition to, and simultaneously with, the issue of summons for service in the manner provided in rules 9 to 19 (both inclusive), also direct the summons to be served by registered post with acknowledgement due addressed to the defendant or his agent empowered to accept the service at the place where the defendant or his agent actually and voluntarily resides and carries on business or personally works for gain. It is the definite case of the respondent that the summons were sent to defendant No. 1 to be served on his constituted attorney defendant No. 5. We have carefully gone through the records of the trial court but we are not find anything to show that this provision of Rule 19B of the Code of Civil Procedure has been complied with. The order sheet is very much silent and even in the record there is no material and we find that actually there was sending of the summons by registered post with acknowledgement due. There is nothing on record to indicate that the postal acknowledgement due was received by the trial court and no step was taken in the miscellaneous case by the respondent to examine the postal peon to prove the service of summons sent by registered post with A/D. It has also been provided in sub-rule (2) of Rule 19B of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure that where the summons were properly addressed pre-paid and duly sent by registered post with acknowledgement due, the declaration referred to in this sub-rule may be made notwithstanding the fact that the acknowledgement having been lost or mislaid or for any other reason, has not been received by the court within thirty days from the date of issue of the summons. This indicate that the Court is required to wait for thirty days from issuance of summons be put for proceeding further which is very much absent in the present case before us. The suit was filed on 29.1.86 and it appears that on the same date summons were handed over to the process server who served the same on 7.6.86 and the suit was decreed on 13.3.86. This fact indicate that there was no compliance of this proviso of sub-rule (2) of Rule 19B of Order 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. All these it appears that has escaped the notice of the trial Court while disposing of the suit ex parte. 

13. Now, from a consideration of the materials on record it appears that by suppressing the summons sent through official process and by not complying with the provision of Rule 19B of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure the ex parte decree has been obtained. It has been held by our Appellate Division in the case of Abul Khair Mia Vs. Abdul Latif Sardar, reported in XXXII D.L.R. (AD) 167, that the ex parte decree obtained by suppressing of summons is a decree obtained fraudulently. Such a decree obtained fraudulently is a nullity. In view of our finding that the decree has been obtained by suppressing of summons and by misleading the Court following the aforesaid decision of our Appellate Division we hold that this decree has been questioned in the miscellaneous case is a nullity. 

14. From the perusal of the record it appears that the process server, O.P.W. 3 submitted a report on the service of summons which cannot be construed and accepted as proper and legal service of summons. This fact was not brought to the notice of the trial Court as it appears in the order-sheet. That the provisions of Rule 19B of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure has not been complied with was not also brought to the notice of the Court and in a post haste an ex parte decree was obtained. This indicate that a fraud was committed upon the Court as well as upon the defendants. This will also be evident from the evidence of O.P.Ws, 2 and 3 who dictated each other on the service of summons which we have discussed above. 

15. The learned Advocate for the respondents submits that the case was not filed within statutory period of time. -- The same was according to him barred by limitation. In 34 D.L.R's. case of our Appellate Division it has been held that when a fraud is proved then there is question of limitation. This will run from the date when the fraud is detected. Here in the present case before us the fraud was proved at the time of disposal of the case 'by the trial Court. So, the question of limitation does not arise. 

16. Furthermore, even if it is found that the fraud was detected earlier a Court is not debarred of any power to interfere in the matter when practice of fraud upon the party as well as upon the Court is detected the civil court can act under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It has been held in the case of Mofazzal Molla & another Vs. Parul Bala Debi & Ors., reported in 24 D.L.R. 78, that as to cases where fraud is committed upon the Court as well as upon the parties, a Court has inherent jurisdiction to interfere in the matter in exercising of its power vested in Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The same view has been expressed in the case of Mozaffar Ahmed & Ors. Vs. Moulvi Saleh Ahmed & Ors, reported in XL D.L.R 239, in the case of Md. Amir Hossain Sarder Vs. Sarat Chandra & Ors. reported In XXXI D.L.R. 109 and in the case of Master Abdul Aziz Vs. Abani Mohan Mukherjee and others, reported in XXX D.L.R. (AD) 221. So, this is the consistent view of the higher Court of this Country that when the fraud is detected and committed either upon the parties or upon the Court is a sufficient ground for civil Court to invoke the provision of Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Here in this case we have already found that a fraud has been com-mitted on the defendant-appellants as well as upon the Court and as such this court can exercise the jurisdiction conferred under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in setting aside the ex parte decree. 

17. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 also questioned the propriety of taking into evidence the power of attorney on the ground that this was duly stamped in this country or revalided as per law. So this document cannot be considered. But it is the consistent view of the higher court of this country that once a document is admitted into evidence its admissibility cannot be questioned in any court at any stage of the same suit on the ground of insufficiency of stamp. In the present case it appears that the power of attorney was taken into evidence without any objection. Now at this stage the respondent was not allowed to raise question on its admissibility. The earnest decision came to our notice on this point in the case of Amin Jute Being Co. Ltd. Vs. Aminpur Union Co-operative Multi-purpose Society Ltd., reported in XII D.L.R. 590. Where it has been held that section 35 of the Stamp Act prohibit a Court from admitting in evidence an instrument which in its view is not duly stamped. This section also prohibits the Court from acting on such document. If the Court however wrongly admits such a document, the appellate Court is prevented by Section 36 of the Stamp Act from calling in question the admission in evidence of such (an Instrument), though it may have been wrongly admitted. This view has been followed in the case of Abul Hashem Vs. Serajul Haque and others, reported in 13 D.L.R. 16 and also in the case of M/s. Boulat Ltd. Vs. Pubali Bank, reported in 39 D.L.R 243. In view of the consistent decisions of the higher court of this Country we hold that the admissibility of the power of attorney cannot now be re-opened at this stage in this Court. 

18. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim also raised in question on the Notarial Act done on the power of attorney. It appears that the power of attorney was notarised by the Notary Public at Peshwar, Pakistan, but before the trial Court nothing has been produced to show that the person who notarised the document has not appointed by the Government of Pakistan as a Notary Public. Mere submission by the learned Advocate will be of no help with-out any material to hold that the person who signed one document as notary public was not appointed as such. It has been held in the case of Nurunnessa and others Vs. Babar Ali Bepari reported in 33 D.L.R. (AD) 124. that notarial acts done by foreign country can be accepted in Bangladesh provided the person before 
whom the notarial act was done as a notary public and the state authorised him to do the notarial act. Here in this present case before us the power of attorney was notarised by notary public at 
Peshwar. Pakistan and there was nothing on record to hold that the person who signed as notary public was not appointed as such by the Government of Pakistan or by the Government of North-South frontier. In that view of the matter we find no force in the argument advanced by Mr. 
Karim in this respect. 

	19. In this matter a further question was raised that the power of attorney was not revalidated in this country. The revalidation was done in the Stamp Acts, if the document is found to be not properly stamped the party concerned get it revalidated or get it properly stamped or the Court itself may impound the document but insufficiency of stamp cannot be a ground to discard a document already taken into evidence. In the 39 D.L.R's case it has been held that the admissibility of such a document cannot be questioned in any Court at any stage of the same suit on the ground of insufficiency of stamp. In view of this decision we find little substance in the submission made by Mr. Karim. 

	20. Thus, after consideration of the materials on record and after hearing the learned Advocate of both the sides and considering the decisions of the higher Courts of this country we hold that a fraud has been committed upon the Court as well as upon the appellant by the plaintiff of the original suit in getting the ex parte decree and as such it requires interference. 

	21. The trial Court took great pains in writing out a very lengthy judgment covering all the points but has overlooked the consistent view of the higher Courts of the subcontinent, more particularly of this country in dealing with such a matter and as such came to a wrong finding which cannot be sustained. 

	22. In view of the aforesaid we hold that this is a fit case where this Court should interfere and set aside the impugned judgment and allow the Miscellaneous Appeal and restored the original suit to its file and number. 

	23. The appeal is allowed. The judgment and order dated 26.8.1991 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra in Miscellaneous Case No 13 of 1987 is hereby set aside and the said case is hereby allowed and the judgment and decree passed in original O.C. Suit No. 46 of 1986 is hereby set aside and the same is restored to its original fine and number. 

	24. The parties will bear their respective costs of the appeal. 

	25. The connected Civil Rule No. 416 - (F.M) of 1991 is hereby discharged as when the appeal is allowed it become anfractuous. 

	26. Let the lower court records be sent down at once.

	End.

lawyer:
Mr. Lokman Karim, Advocate -- For the Petitioner 
Mr. A.S.M. Nazmul Haque, Advocate -- For respondent no. 3
parties:
Mahbub Ali ----- Petitioner
Versus
Artha Rin Adalat-1, Chittagong and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Ullah, J.:- Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order No. 67 dated 01.04.2012(Annexure-G) as well as the judgment and decree dated 27.04.2011 (decree signed on 03.05.2011) (Annexure-E) passed by the Artha Rin Adalat-1, Chittagong in Artha Rin Suit No. 252 of 2004 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

2. Short facts, for the disposal of the Rule, are that the respondent no.2 Sonali Bank Limited, K.C. Dey Road, Corporate Branch, Police Station Kotwali, District Chittagong (hereinafter referred to as the Bank) as plaintiff, on 28.4.2004, instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 252 of 2004 before the Artha Rin Adalat. 10, Court, Chittagong (in short, the Adalat) for recovery of loan amounting to Tk. 5,42,27,515.18 along with interest thereon till realization impleading respondent no. 4, M/S. Mukta Apparels Limited (hereinafter referred to as the respondent-company) and others including the petitioner-Mahbub Ali as defendants of the suit. The defendants entered appearance and filed a joint written statement on 26.7.2005 denying the material averments  made in the plaint. Thereafter, the defendant no. 3- petitioner filed an amended written statement on 23.2.2010 stating, inter alia, that he is mere a Director of the borrower company and he never executed any personal guarantee for the loan and became a Director of the company long after the sanction and disbursement of loan on 14,12.1996. The defendant no.3-petitioner purchased 100 shams from one of the Director of the borrower-company. Md. Nurul Buda, on 11.12.1996 and the plaintiff -Bank approved this defendant no.3-petitioner as Director of the borrower-company on 13.05.1998 according to the decision of its 5815. Board Meeting. The previous Director Md. Nurul Buda resigned born the borrower-company on 18.03.1997. Therefore, the petitioner is not liable for the loan availed by the respondent-company. The petitioner, on 23.2.2010, filed two separate applications. one for accepting the amended written statement and other under section 6(5) read with section 57 of the Ain, 2003 (in short the AM, 2003), for striking out of his name from the plaint of Artha Rin Suit No. 252 of 2004 but the learned judge of the Adalat continued the proceeding of the suit without disposal of the said two applications. Therefore, the petitioner filed a Writ Petition being No. 3520 of 2010 before this Court seeking a direction upon the Artha Rin Adalat for disposed of the applications filed by the petitioner on 23.2.2010 before further proceeding of the suit and the said writ petition was disposed of summarily on 09.05.2010 with a direction to the learned judge of the Adalat to consider and dispose of the applications dated 23.02,2010 filed by the defendant no. 3-petitioner before further proceeding of the Artha Rin Suit. Thereafter Adalat upon hearing the parties, rejected the said applications filed by the respondent no. 3-petitioner vide its order no. 50 dated 13.05.2010. Then the petitioner filed another Writ Petition being No. 4010 of 2010 challenging the decision dated 13.05.2010 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Chittagong in Artha Rin Suit No. 252 of 2004 and Rule was issued but subsequently the same was discharged on 01.02.2011 with certain observations. Then the Adalat framed Additional issues to the effect whether the defendant no. 3 executed any personal guarantee, whether the defendant 00. 3 is liable for the loan, and whether the share of the defendant no. 3 would be liable for repayment of the loan liability. Thereafter, the Artha Rin Adalat by its Judgment and order dated 27.4.2011 decreed the suit (decree signed on 3.5.2011) against all the defendants including the petitioner for claimed amount of Tk. 5,42,27,515.18 to be paid by the defendant Nos. 1-4 jointly within 60 days failing which the decree holder bank would realize the same with 12% interest till realization thereof. Thereafter, on 20.2.2012, the petitioner filed an application under section 57 of the AM, 2003 for deleting the name of the petitioner from the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Suit dated 27.4.2011 and 3.5.2011 respectively by way of correction of the same and the Adalat, by one of the impugned order dated 01.04.2012, rejected the said application of the petitioner holding that since against the judgment of the Artha Rin Adalat alternative remedy for preferring an appeal is available, the application under section 57 of the AM, 2003 for correction of the judgment and decree is not maintainable. Therefore, the petitioner approached this Court and obtained the present Rule as stated above. 

3. Mr. Lokman Karim, learned Advocate, drawing our attention to the case of Md. Arfan Uddin Akand vs. Joint District judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.1 Gazipur and another, heard and disposed of along with Writ Petition No. 6930 of 2004, reported in 15 BLT(2007) 343, and Fariduddin Mahmud Vs. Md. Saidur Rahman and others, reported in 63 DLR(AD)93, submits that if the Adalat passes any order which is wholly without jurisdiction, in other words in excess of jurisdiction, then despite the fact that the law provided forum for appeal, the petitioner cannot be debarred from availing the writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution and as such the instant Writ Petition is maintainable since the Adalat acted without jurisdiction in passing the impugned judgment and decree so far against the petitioner is concerned as the Adalat found that the petitioner never executed personal guarantee and signed any charge document for the loan availed by the respondent-company. 

4. Mr. Karim submits further that prior to sanction of the loan dated 22.11.1995 in favour of the respondent-company, the petitioner was neither Director nor guarantor and even nor a share-holder of the company and in that admitted situation the petitioner ought not to have been made a party in the Artha Rin Suit in view of the provision of sub-section(5) of Section 6 of the Ain, 2003 and as such the impugned judgment and decree, so far the petitioner is concerned, is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

5. Mr. A.S.M. Nazmul Haque, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent no. 3-Sonali Bank, by filing an affidavit-in-opposition, on the other hand, submits that the petitioner is not competent to challenge the legality and propriety of the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat under writ jurisdiction and the remedy if any, lies for the petitioner to prefer an appeal in an appropriate Court. In such view of the matter, the Rule beats no merit and it should be discharged, he submits. Mr. Haque, learned Advocate, submits further that the writ petition involving the disputed question of facts, cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction and as such the Rule should be discharged. Mr. Haque, lastly submits that the defendant no.3-petitoner filed joint written statement with other defendants and thereby assumed the jurisdiction of the Artha Rin Adalat and as such he cannot escape himself from the jurisdiction of the Adalat at this stage. 

6. We have heard the learned Advocates from both the parties perused the materials on record including the writ petition, annexure there to, affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent no.3 Sonali Bank and have gone through the decisions as referred to. 

7. It appears that the loan was sanctioned on 22.11.1995 in favour of the respondent-company while petitioner purchased 100 share from one of the Director of the borrower company, S.M. Nurul Huda, on 11.12.1996 and the respondent no. 2 lender Bank approved this petitioner as Director of the borrower-company on 13.0,5.1998 by its 586, Board Meeting. It further appears that the Adalat found that the petitioner did not execute any charge document for the purpose of taking liability of loan availed by the respondent-company. The findings of the Adalat about the execution of charge document, so far the petitioner is concerned, is as follows: “চার্জ ডকুমেন্ট ৩ নং বিবাদীর স্বাক্ষর না থাকিলেও পরবর্তীতে কোম্পানীর নিযুক্ত হওয়ায় তিনি বাদী ব্যাংকের দেনার জন্য ১০০ শেয়ারের মালিক হিসাবে ২০% দেনা পরিশোধ করিতে বাধ্য।” 

8. Although the petitioner without understanding the situation filed joint written statement with other defendants denying the material allegation of the plaint, but, subsequently, he filed two applications, one was for amendment of the written statement and other for striking out the name of the petitioner from the plaint of Artha Rin Suit. When the Adana proceeded with the suit without disposing of those applications, the petitioner obtained an order of this Court invoking writ jurisdiction for disposal of the said applications at first. When the Adalat rejected those applications of the petitioner, he further moved this Court and filed Writ Petition No. 4010 of 2010 whereupon Rule was issued and subsequently was discharged with the following observations: 

"However, while disposing the suit on merit the learned judge of the Artha Rin Adalat should examine as to whether defendant No. 3-petitoner executed any personal guarantee for the loan or his loan liability is limited to his shares of the Company as well as the property owned by the Company." 

9. The High Court Division by its aforesaid observations firstly observed that the Adalat should ascertain whether the defendant no.3 petitioner executed any personal guarantee for the loan availed by the respondent-company and if it is found negative, the petitioner was required to he discharged or released from the alleged liability brought by the respondent-Bank in the suit against the petitioner. But if it is found that the petitioner executed any letter of guarantee, he will never be discharged from the liability of the loan taken by the respondent company. The Adalat on consideration of the evidence on record found that the defendant no. 3 petitioner did not execute any personal guarantee for taking liability of the loan at any point of time. This being so, Adalat ought to have dismissed the suit against the petitioner is concerned. 

10. A company incorporated under the companies Act is a juristic person. A share holder is not the owner of the company or its assets. The company itself owns its property. A share-holder is only entitled to the dividends, if declared. On winding up however after payment of its debts he is entitled to participate in the distribution of its assets. It is no doubt, the liability of a. share-holder, whether he is the Chairman of the Board of Directors, or a director, is only to the extent of the face value of the shares he holds nothing more than that. But a share-holder of a
company is not a necessary party in the Artha Rin Suit. The chairman or the directors or any other guarantor who executed the charge document in respect of payment of loan are liable and are necessary parties in the Artha Rin Suit for the purpose of effectual adjudication of the matter between the loanee company and the financial institutions. Chairman or director, if he did not execute any charge document, he or she shall not be liable for the loan save and except their liability to the extent of the face value of the shares he/she holds. 

11. It appears that, admittedly, defendant no. 3-petitioner was neither a borrower nor guarantor and even nor a mortgagor relating to the loan liability and, therefore, he is not liable for repayment of the loan inasmuch as the petitioner does not come within the purview of sub-section (5) of section 6 of the AM, 2003, wherein who will be the necessary party in the Artha Rin suit has been provided, and - hence the suit ought to have been dismissed as against this defendant no. 3- petitioner. For better understanding sub-section (5) of section 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 is quoted below: 
“৬।(১)...........................................
(২)................................................
(৩)...............................................
(৪)...............................................
(৫)আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান মূল ঋণগ্রহিতার (Principal debtor) বিরুদেধ মামলা দায়ের করার সময় তৃতীয় পক্ষ বন্ধকদাতা (Third Party mortgagor) বা তৃতীয় পক্ষ গ্রারান্টার (Third party guarantor) ঋণের সহিত সংশ্লিষ্ট থাকিলে উহাদিগেকে বিবাদী পক্ষ করিবে এবং আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত রায় আদেশ বা ডিক্রি সকল বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে যৌথভাবে ও পৃথক পৃথকভাবে (Jointly and severally) কার্যকর হইবে এবং ডিক্রী জাররি মামলা সকল বিবাদী দায়িকের বিরুদ্ধে একই সাথে পরিচালিত হইবেঃ
তবে শর্ত থাকে যে ডিত্রি জাবীর মাধ্যমে দাবী আদায় হওয়ার ক্ষেত্রে আদালত প্রথমে মূল ঋণ-গ্রহীতা বিবাদীর েএবং অতঃপর যখাক্রমে তৃতীয় পক্ষ বন্ধকদাতা (Third Party mortgagor) ও তৃতীয় পক্ষ গ্রারান্টার (Third party guarantor) এর সম্পত্তি যতদুর সম্ভব আকৃষ্ট করিবেঃ
আরো শর্ত থাকে যে বাদীর অনুকুলৈ প্রদত্ত ডিক্রির দাবী তৃতীয় পক্ষ বন্ধকদাতা (Third Party mortgagor)অথবা তৃতীয় পক্ষ গ্রারান্টর (Third party guarantor) পরিশোধ করিয়া থাকিলে উক্ত ডিক্রি যখাক্রমে তাহাদের অনুকুলে স্থানান্তরিত হইবে এবং তাহারা মূল ঋণগ্রহীতার (Principal debtor) বিরুদ্ধে উহা প্রয়োগ বা জারী করিতে পারিবেন।”

12. The Adalat at the time of passing any judgment or finally disposing of the suit should have to take into consideration of the fads as to whether the plaintiff-financial institution made the defendant/defendants in the Artha Rin Suit in view of the statutory provision of sub-section(5) of section 6 of the Ain. 2003 and also to determine whether the defendant in the Artha Rin Suit is a borrower or mortgagor or guarantor for the purpose of fixing the liability of the loan taken by a company, for different business purpose, from the plaintiff-financial institution. When the Adalat passed the impugned judgment beyond the scope of law as provided for in section 6(5) of the Ain, 2003, then it can be said that the same is without jurisdiction. 

13. However the teamed Advocate for the respondent-Bank, drawing our attention to the joint written statement filed by the defendants including the petitioner, submits that the petitioner assumed the jurisdiction of the Artha Kin Adalat, so at a later stage he cannot escape or say he was not a necessary party in the Artha Rin Suit. It is settled principle that jurisdiction of a Court cannot be coddled upon consent of the parties, it is the statute only which can confer the jurisdiction of the Court. When the petitioner filed written statement without understanding the legal consequence with the other defendants it does not mean that he assumed the jurisdiction of the Artha Rin Adalat unless and until it is found that he is a necessary party in the Artha Rin Suit in view of the provision of sub-section (5) of Section 6 of the AM, 2003. Further, when the defendant no.3 petitioner was in no way connected with the loan in question, as the loan was taken before his joining to the ounce company and that the petitioner never executed any letter of guarantee to secure the loan, in this situation the judgment and decree of the Adalat directing the petitioner with other defendants jointly to pay Tk.5,42,27,515.I8 is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect so far the petitioner is concerned. We cannot shut our eyes when there is error apparent on the face of the record or where the decision of the Adalat is vitiated by malafide or the Adalat acted in excess of jurisdiction or acted contrary to the fundamental principles or acted with malice in law. In that case, despite the alternative remedy, writ jurisdiction can be invoked under Article 102 of the Constitution. 

14. Regard being had to the above discussions of law and facts, we are of the view that the Rule has substance and as such the same should succeed. 

15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute in part, however without any order as to costs. 

16. Accordingly, the judgment and decree dated 27.4.2011 (decree signed on 03.05.2011) passed by the learned Artha Rin Adalat No. I, Chittagong in Artha Rin Suit No. 252 of 2004 is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect so far the petitioner is concerned only. 

17. Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No.1 Chittagong.

End.
